## Library Services

**USERS AND BORROWING PRIVILEGES**

|     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Category of Users** | **No. of Books** | **Period of Loan** |
| Students UG and PG | 03 | 15 days |
| SC-ST Students | 04 | 15 days |
| Teaching Faculty | 08 | One Month |
| Non-Teaching Staff | 03 | 15 days |
| Research Scholar | 05 | One Month |

- The Book must be returned on or before the due date. After the due date Rs. 1 / day will be charged.
- Borrowers are to produce their ID card when borrowing resource materials.
- ID cards are not transferable. Use of an ID card is restricted to the user to whom the card is issued.
- Members must satisfy themselves about the physical conditions of the library material being issued. They shall be held responsible for any damage/mutilation noticed at the time of return.

**Lending:**

Lending books will be issued to the students for defined days. Books so lent shall be returned on due date **.**

\[Lending books are available in Ground Flour Stack Area\]

**Reference:**

Reference books will not be issued to the users.

\[Reference books are available in First Flour Reading Section Area\]

**Digital Library:**

Library provides the internet connected computer systems to access the E-Databases, E- Journals, E-Books, other subscribed e- resources and internet browsing for users.

**_Institutional Repository:_**

ATMECE Library established the ‘Institutional Repository’ which has e-books, Question Papers and faculty publications, and Project reports to access remotely.

**_E-Resource Subscription Access:_**

ATMECE is member of VTU Consortium, through the consortium library provides the access to subscribed

- E-Content(e-journals/e-books/Etc.) and
- Technology Platforms (Plagiarism / Grammar / Remote Access Tools/Etc.)

**Multimedia:**

CD/DVDs including Project reports and Textbooks and other resourceful service is available for users.

**OPAC (Online Public Access Catalogue):**

OPAC (library catalogue) allows the users to search the library books. The library catalogue is searched by author, title, and keyword.

**Question Papers:**

The library facilitates to access the previous year’s exam question paper in electronic format available in our Institutional Repository for reference purpose.

**Periodical:**

1. **E-Journals**
2. **Print-Journals**
3. **Magazines/Newspapers**

ATME College of Engineering is rated ‘GOLD’ by QS I·GAUGE for its Overall Excellence as a top-notch College. As one of the best rated College in Mysuru, ATME College of Engineering has been excelling in the field of education for more than 10 years.

ATME is proud to receive QS I·GAUGE ‘GOLD’ rating for its overall excellence and has become the 1st College in Mysuru to be awarded in Engineering Category.

While the entire nation is trapped under the threat of corona virus pandemic, ATME College is striving constantly to maintain a global benchmark in imparting first-rate education. Through an overabundance of its unique programs, the college is helping students leverage the most out of their degrees, I·GAUGE is a brand incorporated in India as an independent private-sector initiative specialized in rating colleges and universities. It brings together the global expertise, experience, and reputation of United Kingdom (UK) based Quacquarelli Symonds (QS), along with deep local knowledge of luminaries from Indian Higher Education. Based on the globally recognized QS STARS University Rating System developed by QS, QS I·GAUGE has been adapted to capture the reality of the dynamic Indian higher education sector, while at the same time maintaining the strict quality standards that are synonymous with the QS brand.

cseds-mentoring-module.markdown:
[Skip to content](/p/cseds-mentoring-module) [![ATME College of Engineering](/__l5e/assets-v1/4519b204-1c5c-4570-ad02-6e238e674849/ATME-Final-logo-copy.png)](/p/) ## Mentoring Module **Process of Mentoring** A maximum of 40-45 students are allotted to each Mentor. The Mentor shall record and maintainthe details of each student in Academic Information Management System (AIMS). **Academic Information Management System (AIMS):** The utilization of AIMS for recording and maintaining student details is a smart approach. AIMS provides a centralized platform where mentors can store academic records, personal interests, progress assessments, and any special considerations for each student. This digital system aids in organized tracking and ensures easy access to relevant information when planning mentoring sessions. **Mentoring frequency** The Mentor will schedule about three to four interactive sessions with students. **1st Mentoring Session will comprise the following points (Before IA test-1):** - Mentors will collect the List of Advanced, Average and Slow Learners from the class - Discuss about the students Interests, Hobbies and their inclination towards curricular, co-curricular and extracurricular - Discussion of previous semester’s Academic Discussion on importance of internal tests and attendance. - Enquire about the preparations for the 1st Internal **2nd Mentoring Meet (Before IA test-2):** Discuss about the 1st IA performance with respect to courses. If the student performanceis unsatisfactory, then reasons for their low scoring are discussed and accordingly suggestions are given. Students are encouraged to participate in co-curricular and extracurricular activities. **3rd Mentoring Meet (Before IA test-3):** Discuss about the 2nd IA performance with respect to courses. If the student performance is unsatisfactory, then reasons for their low scoring are discussed and accordingly suggestions are given. Students will be advised to attend the 3 IA compulsorily and to prepare action plan for the Semester End Exam preparation **4th Mentoring Meet (After IA test-3 Optional):** Non-compliance of any points raised in the above mentoring sessions will Students will be advised on the above **Note: The Internal Assessment performance and attendance status of each student will be communicated to the respective parents.** **Mentor-Allotted Student Groups:** The allocation of 45 students to each mentor ensures a manageable and personalized approach. With a smaller group, mentors can devote more attention to understanding each student’s needs, strengths, and areas for improvement. This arrangement facilitates effective mentor-student relationships and allows mentors to offer more individualized guidance. **Academic Information Management System (AIMS):** The utilization of AIMS for recording and maintaining student details is a smart approach. AIMS provides a centralized platform where mentors can store academic records, personal interests, progress assessments, and any special considerations for each student. This digital system aids in organized tracking and ensures easy access to relevant information when planning mentoring sessions. **Mentoring Frequency:** The plan to schedule three to four interactive sessions per student is beneficial for several reasons. Regular interaction enables mentors to closely monitor students’ progress and address any challenges or concerns promptly. These sessions can involve discussing academic goals, study techniques, clarifying doubts, and exploring personal interests. The frequency ensures consistent support and guidance throughout the academic term. **1** **st** **Mentoring Session will comprise the following points (Before IA test 1):** - Mentors will collect the List of Advanced, Average and Slow Learners from the class. - Discuss about the students Interests, Hobbies and their inclination towards curricular, co-curricular and extracurricular. - Discussion of previous semester’s Academic Discussion on importance of internal tests and attendance. - Enquire about the preparations for the 1st Internal **2nd Mentoring Meet (Before IA test 2):** - Discuss about the 1st IA performance with respect to courses. If the student performance is unsatisfactory, then reasons for their low scoring are discussed and accordingly suggestions are given. - Students are encouraged to participate in co-curricular and extracurricular activities for various. - Discussion on Attendance status. **3rd Mentoring Meet (Before IA test 3):** - Discuss about the 2nd IA performance with respect to courses. If the student performance is unsatisfactory, then reasons for their low scoring are discussed and accordingly suggestions are given. - Students will be advised to attend the 3 IA compulsorily and to prepare action plan for the Semester End Exam preparation. - Discussion on Attendance status. **4th Mentoring Meet (After IA test-3 Optional):** - Non-compliance of any points raised in the above mentoring sessions will. - Students will be advised on the above **Note: The Internal Assessment performance and attendance status of each student will be communicated to the respective parents.** | | | | --- | --- | | ###### **Maximum No. of Students**

In a flipped classroom, students engage with instructional content, such as video lectures or readings, outside of class. This pre-class preparation frees up in-class time for interactive activities, discussions, and problem-solving. It fosters deeper understanding through real-time interactions with peers and instructors and prepares students for real-world application of knowledge. The contents are shared to the learners through Microsoft Teams. ![](/__l5e/assets-v1/b5900c1d-6557-4665-92ca-c0d971b6ea56/flip-1024x576.png) #### [Lab Videos](/p/cseds-innovative-teaching-learning-methods) | | | | --- | --- | | **Gen AI-(BAIL657C)** | | Program 1 | GenerativeAI Lab - YouTube

cse-data-science-2.description: I'm delighted to be the Head of Data Science at ATMECE Mysore . Our department is equipped with an excellent, passionate faculty team who are all thoroughly
cse-data-science-2.markdown:
[Skip to content](/p/cse-data-science-2)

[![ATME College of Engineering](/__l5e/assets-v1/4519b204-1c5c-4570-ad02-6e238e674849/ATME-Final-logo-copy.png)](/p/)

![](/__l5e/assets-v1/80d096c4-a6d7-4541-b781-5dafd5dcfac0/WhatsApp-Image-2023-02-15-at-2.01.36-PM-1200x600.jpeg)

## Department of CSE – Data Science

#### About the Department

I’m delighted to be the Head of Data Science at ATMECE Mysore . Our department is equipped with an excellent, passionate faculty team who are all thoroughly qualified and up-to-date on the latest industry trends. Our students are highly motivated and well-trained for the IT sector with hands-on experience in cutting edge technologies and programming languages.

I’m confident that our students will not only attain good academic score but will also acquire high-paying jobs. The scientific examination of data using mathematical and statistical models, machine learning tools, and artificial intelligence is called data science. In present scenario data scientists play very vital role in deriving conclusions and recommendations in various domains to make our life a better life Department is equipped all modern tools and technologies to impart knowledge in the field of Data Science. Our institute facilitates students with placement training in aptitude and technical sessions, as well as soft-skill classes to aid in better placement.

We at ATMECE more importance is placed on elevating the students learning experience by providing value-added courses, skill-enhancement programs, and motivate students to participate in technical symposiums, hackathons organised by premier institutes across the nation. I am confident that the Department of Data Science students at ATMECE is prepared to face the new societal issues and challenges in this new millennium ,we transform our students  in all dimensions of their student life to become better citizen of this nation for better India and better world.

**[![](/__l5e/assets-v1/3fdc57b3-0ae6-4775-8558-f81d3cad1452/Anitha-D-B-1.jpg)](/p/cse-data-science/cse-faculty-profile-data-science/anitha-d-b-1)**

**Dr. Anitha D B**

**Associate Professor & Head CSE-DS(Data Science)**

#### [Vision of the Department](/p/cse-data-science-2)

To impart technical education in the field of data science of excellent quality with a high level of professional competence, social responsibility, and global awareness among the students.

#### [Mission of the Department](/p/cse-data-science-2)

- To impart technical education that is up to date, relevant and makes students competitive and employable at global level
- To provide technical education with a high sense of discipline, social relevance in an intellectually, ethically and socially challenging environment for better tomorrow
- Educate to the global standards with a benchmark of excellence and to kindle the spirit


of innovation.

#### [Program Educational Objectives (PEOs)](/p/cse-data-science-2)

- **PEO1:** Develop cutting-edge skills in data science and its related technologies, such as machine learning, predictive analytic, and data engineering.
- **PEO2:** Design and develop data-driven solutions to real-world problems in a business, research, or social environment.
- **PEO3:** Apply data engineering and data visualization techniques to discover, investigate, and interpret data.
- **PEO4:** Demonstrate ethical and responsible data practices in problem solving
- **PEO5:** Integrate fields within computer science, optimization, and statistics to develop better solutions

#### [Program Specific objectives (PSOs)](/p/cse-data-science-2)

- **PSO1:** Develop relevant programming skills to become a successful data scientist
- **PSO2:** Apply data science concepts and algorithms to solve real world problems of the society
- **PSO3:** Apply data science techniques in the various domains like agriculture, education healthcare for better society

#### [Program Outcomes (POs)](/p/cse-data-science-2)

01. **Engineering knowledge**: Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.
02. **Problem analysis:** Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.
03. **Design/development of solutions:** Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for the public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental


    considerations.
04. **Conduct investigations of complex problems:** Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions.
05. **Modern tool usage:** Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools including prediction and modeling to complex engineering activities with an understanding of the limitations.
06. **The engineer and society:** Apply reasoning informed by the contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to the professional engineering practice.
07. **Environment and sustainability:** Understand the impact of the professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for sustainable development.
08. **Ethics:** Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the engineering practice.
09. **Individual and team work:** Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams, and in multidisciplinary settings.
10. **Communication:** Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and with society at large, such as, being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations, and give and receive clear instructions.
11. **Project management and finance:** Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the engineering and management principles and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.
12. **Life-long learning:** Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.

csd-training-internship.markdown:

By offering hands-on workshops, industry-relevant courses, and expert mentorship, SKULLERR equips individuals with the skills needed to excel in the fast-paced tech industry. Specializing in areas like software development and Cyber Security, the platform ensures students stay ahead with an evolving curriculum and career-focused support, including job placement assistance and networking opportunities. SKULLERR is dedicated to turning tech aspirations into achievements, helping individuals launch and advance their careers. The startup is also MSME registered with a registration No. UDYAM-KR-22-0047609. ![](/__l5e/assets-v1/186afa41-c3bb-485c-92a7-c58a0acd0f27/skul.png) ![](/__l5e/assets-v1/54428f36-862f-4a74-95a8-e98d65eb435f/awards.png) ![](/__l5e/assets-v1/7eb6caa9-04b4-4e61-9e58-154589ba446e/cert-1024x709.png) **Ms. Madhurya H V** a 2nd year student was awarded as the **Best Presenter in National Level Paper Presentation** Held at Bangalore Technological Institute, Bangalore on **25 April 2025.** She presented a paper titled **“Quantum Satellites-The Future of Unhackable Communication”.** * * * #### **Student Achievements - Finalist in Smart India Hackathon 2023** | | | | | | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Sl. AICTE Scholarship schemes for BE, BCA & MBA students.](/p/scholarships) | | | | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | **AICTE-YASHASVI:(‘YOUNG ACHIEVERS  SCHOLARSHIP SCHEME’**
A scholarship scheme from AICTE for meritorious students seeking admission in core branches of Engineering in order to motivate students to pursue engineering education in the core branches of engineering. | [https://facilities.aicte-india.org/FAQsYashasvi%20Scheme\_2024.pdf](https://facilities.aicte-india.org/FAQsYashasvi%20Scheme_2024.pdf) | | 2 | **'AICTE – SWANATH SCHOLARSHIP SCHEME**
for children from any one of the following categories:1. Orphan, 2. Either or both parents died due to Covid-19
3\. Wards of Armed Forces and Central Paramilitary Forces martyred in action (Shaheed) to provide them financial support for every year of study. | [https://www.aicte-india.org/sites/default/files/stdc/AICTE-SWANATH-%20SCHEME-DEGREE-DIPLOMA.pdf](https://www.aicte-india.org/sites/default/files/stdc/AICTE-SWANATH-%20SCHEME-DEGREE-DIPLOMA.pdf) | | 3 | **AICTE PRAGATHI SCHOLARSHIP**
Scholarship/Contingency is awarded to meritorious girls taking admission in AICTE approved Technical institution at Degree/ Diploma. | [https://www.aicte-india.org/schemes/students-development-schemes/Pragati/General-Instructions](https://www.aicte-india.org/schemes/students-development-schemes/Pragati/General-Instructions) | | 4 | **AICTE SARASWATI SCHEME**
A scholarship scheme from AICTE for meritorious girls students perusing **BBA/BMS/BCA** Courses in AICTE Approved Institutions. | [https://facilities.aicte-india.org/AICTE%20Saraswati%20Scholarship%20Scheme%20Guidelines\_2024-Final.pdf](https://facilities.aicte-india.org/AICTE%20Saraswati%20Scholarship%20Scheme%20Guidelines_2024-Final.pdf) | | 5 | **AICTE  SAKSHAM SCHOLARSHIP**
Scholarship/Contingency is awarded to Differently abled students taking admission in AICTE approved Technical institution at Degree/ Diploma. | [https://www.aicte-india.org/schemes/students-development-schemes/Saksham/General-Instructions](https://www.aicte-india.org/schemes/students-development-schemes/Saksham/General-Instructions) | | 6 | **AICTE PG SCHOLARSHIP SCHEME**
The AICTE offers a Post Graduate Scholarship Scheme for GATE/GPAT qualified students admitted to AICTE-approved postgraduate programs. This scheme provides a monthly stipend of ₹12,400 per student to encourage higher education in technical fields. | [https://www.aicte-india.org/schemes/students-development-schemes/PG-Scholarship-Scheme](https://www.aicte-india.org/schemes/students-development-schemes/PG-Scholarship-Scheme) | ### [II. NSP- National Scholarship Portal](/p/scholarships) | | | | | --- | --- | --- | | **1** | **Dept. of Higher Education:**
**1.PRADHAN MANTRI UCHCHATAR SHIKSHA PROTSAHAN (PM-USP) YOJANA**
To provide financial assistance to meritorious students from poor families to meet a part of their day-to-day expenses while pursuing higher studies | [**https://scholarships.gov.in/public/schemeGuidelines/CSSS\_GUIDLINES\_07022024\_updated.pdf**](https://scholarships.gov.in/public/schemeGuidelines/CSSS_GUIDLINES_07022024_updated.pdf) | | **2** | **DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL JUSTICE & EMPOWERMENT** **.**
The Scheme aims at recognizing and promoting quality education amongst students belonging to SCs, by providing financial support. The Scheme will cover SC students for pursuing studies beyond 12th class | [**https://scholarships.gov.in/public/schemeGuidelines/Top\_Class\_Education\_Scheme\_2018.pdf**](https://scholarships.gov.in/public/schemeGuidelines/Top_Class_Education_Scheme_2018.pdf) | | **3** | **NATIONAL SCHOLARSHIP FOR POSTGRADUATE STUDIES**
The scholarships under these schemes shall be available for pursuing PG degree programme | [**https://scholarships.gov.in/public/schemeGuidelines/Guidelines\_NATIONAL\_SCHOLARSHIP\_FOR\_POSTGRADUATE\_STUDIES\_UGC\_2324.pdf**](https://scholarships.gov.in/public/schemeGuidelines/Guidelines_NATIONAL_SCHOLARSHIP_FOR_POSTGRADUATE_STUDIES_UGC_2324.pdf) | | **4** | **PM YASASVI CENTRAL SECTOR SCHEME**
The objective of the scheme is to recognize and promote quality education amongst Students belonging to OBC, EBC and DNT categories by providing full financial support **.** | [**https://scholarships.gov.in/public/schemeGuidelines/ApprovedmodifieddraftofTopClassCollege.pdf**](https://scholarships.gov.in/public/schemeGuidelines/ApprovedmodifieddraftofTopClassCollege.pdf) | | **5** | **CENTRAL SECTOR UMBRELLA SCHEME OF "SCHOLARSHIPS FOR STUDENTS WITH DISABILITIES"** | [**https://scholarships.gov.in/public/schemeGuidelines/DEPDGuidelines\_1.pdf**](https://scholarships.gov.in/public/schemeGuidelines/DEPDGuidelines_1.pdf)
**OR**
[**https://depwd.gov.in/**](https://depwd.gov.in/) | ### [III. AICTE Fellowship schemes for BE, BCA & MBA students](/p/scholarships) | | | | | --- | --- | --- | | **1** | **AICTE PRODUCTIZATION FELLOWSHIP (APF** AICTE )
Productization Fellowship (APF) is a new initiative of AICTE, with the objective to support Innovative Ideas that drive future economic growth and contribute to the Nations Vision of “ATMANIRBHAR BHARAT” and “VIKSIT BHARAT@ 2047” | [**https://facilities.aicte-india.org/downloads/APF%20Scheme%20Guidlines.pdf**](https://facilities.aicte-india.org/downloads/APF%20Scheme%20Guidlines.pdf) | | **2** | **AICTE POST-DOCTORAL FELLOWSHIP (PDF) 2024-25**
AICTE Post-Doctoral Fellowship is to encourage Indian Engineering, Management, Design, Applied Sciences, Planning, Computer application, Inter Disciplinary Area scholars who have completed their Ph.D and wish to pursue a regular career in research and development. | [**https://www.aicte-india.org/sites/default/files/AICTE%20PDF%20scheme%20Guidelines.pdf**](https://www.aicte-india.org/sites/default/files/AICTE%20PDF%20scheme%20Guidelines.pdf) | | **3** | **AICTE AURA(AUGMENTING UTILIZATION OF RESEARCH ASSETS) 2024 SCHEME**
AICTE AURA (Augmenting Utilization of Research Assets) 2024, by providing the financial aid to AICTE approved institutions, students of PG Scholarship Scheme/ ADF Scheme/ QIP Scheme of AICTE and all students of Under Graduate/ Post Graduate studying in AICTE approved Institutions to boost research and mobility of researchers. | [**https://www.aicte-india.org/sites/default/files/AICTE%20AURA%202024%20SCHEME\_GUIDELINES.pdf**](https://www.aicte-india.org/sites/default/files/AICTE%20AURA%202024%20SCHEME_GUIDELINES.pdf) | | **4** | **“AICTE-Vishwakarma Awards-2020”**
To recognize and honour the innovative work of the students displaying exceptional skills in different categories. | [**https://www.aicte-india.org/AICTE%20Vishwakarma%20Award%202020**](https://www.aicte-india.org/AICTE%20Vishwakarma%20Award%202020) | | **5** | **Smart India Hackathon:**

## Co-curricular & Extracurricular Activities

#### REPORT on Student Club Inauguration and Technical Talk

The Department of CSE (Data Science) launched its technical club _**DataNauts**_ on 14 th May 2025 at AB401, in the presence of Dr. Basavaraj L (Principal), Dr. Anitha D B (Associate Professor & HOD), and Mr. Yogabalaji G, Decision Scientist at Mu Sigma Inc., Bengaluru.

As part of the launch, a technical talk on **“How Data is used to Build Solutions and Maximizing Efficiency”** was conducted for 4 th and 6 th semester students, coordinated by the staff members of the department and students.

## Industry Interface

**Industry Visit to Skanray Technologies Pvt. Ltd. — Department of CSE (Data Science)**

**Date of Visit:** 12th April 2025

**Department:**Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science) – 4th Semester Students

**Institution:** ATME College of Engineering, Mysuru

**Industry Visit Convenor  –  Dr. Anitha D B,-** Associate Professor & Head , Department of CSE (Data Science)

**Accompanying Faculty Members:– Dr. Vinod Kumar P** – Associate Professor , Department of CSE (Data Science)

The Department of Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science), ATMECE,Mysuru organized an enriching **Industrial Visit** to **Skanray Technologies Pvt. Ltd., Mysuru**, a leading innovator in the medical equipment manufacturing industry, on **12th April 2025**.

During the visit, students gained valuable insights into the **design, development, and production** of cutting-edge healthcare technologies, including:

- Advanced **ventilators**

- **Medical imaging systems**

- **Patient monitoring devices**


The visit offered students a unique opportunity to witness firsthand how **engineering innovation** meets **real-world healthcare needs** through a strong focus on **quality, precision, and technological excellence**. Interacting with industry professionals and observing real-time processes provided practical exposure that will greatly enhance their academic and professional journeys.

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Industry-Visit_01-225x300.jpg)![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/INdustry-Visit_02-300x225.jpg)

The Department extends its heartfelt gratitude to  the entire **Skanray Technologies** team for their support, guidance, and warm hospitality, making this visit a highly impactful learning experience. Such initiatives help bridge the gap between classroom learning and industry practices, inspiring students to pursue excellence in the evolving field of **Medical Technology and Data Science**.

## Campus Security

#### [CCTV](/p/security)

Video Surveillance or CCTV are used to observe an area and connected to a recording device or IP Network and monitored in a [Server](http://ifsecglobal.staging.wpengine.com/control-rooms/) Room. CCTV’s are placed at the strategic locations in the campus to keep track of situations in Campus.

**No. of CCTV’s in Campus- 140**

#### [SECURITY PERSONNEL](/p/security)

The security section of the institute is entrusted to provide security and safety to all the people on campus including students, faculty and staff members and security personnel also work for the safety of assets on the campus.

- Security Persons will regulate and maintain traffic, both vehicular and pedestrian on the campus.
- Will ensure that the campus is free from trespassers and squatters, to deal with defaulters if any inappropriate manners.
- To deal with entry/exit of departments, sections, offices excess control of which have been entrusted to Security Section.

#### [FIRE EXTINGUISHER](/p/security)

ATME College of Engineering provides fire extinguishers which is an active fire protection device used to extinguish or control small fires, often in emergency situations. Typically, a fire extinguisher consists of a hand-held cylindrical pressure vessel containing an agent which can be discharged to extinguish a fire. Fire extinguishers manufactured with non-cylindrical pressure vessels also exist but are less common.

**No. of Fire Extinguishers in Campus- 37**

#### [FIRST AID FACILITY](/p/security)

First aid is the assistance given to any person suffering a serious illness or injury, with care provided to preserve life, prevent the condition from worsening, or to promote recovery.

atmece-donated-semi-fowler-bed-to-distri.markdown:

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/46.jpg)

## ATMECE Donated semi Fowler bed to District Administration for COVID Care.

ATME College of Engineering has extending its helping hand to the District authorities in its fight against COVID by donating 75 No of Semi fowler bed worth Rs.10.18 Lakh to take care of COVID 19 patients.

Responding to the call of the District authorities to Industrialist and Philanthropists to join hands in strengthening the Mysore City’s health infrastructure, Management of ATME College of Engineering immediately rose to the occasion and contributed towards it.  Amid lockdown and non-availability of men and materials ATME College identified and persuaded the vendor to supply 75 No of Semi Fowler beds.

Speaking on the occasion Sri. Arun Kumar L, Chairman of ATME College of Engineering said he is deeply moved by the suffering of the COVID 19 patients in the recent times in getting proper health care. Sensing the of the overburdening of the Health Infrastructure, he decided to make a small contribution towards city’s health infrastructure.

ATME Charitable Trust, which is managing ATME College of Engineering, is a philanthropic organization, involved in many Humanitarian, Benevolent and Socially Responsible activities.

Every year ATME College of Engineering Celebrates its Annual fest with a Social Responsibility theme thereby inculcating sense of responsibility towards the society among its students.

Every year College is Organises free blood camp, free health Check-ups and Free Eye Check-ups in Collaboration with NSS and Red Cross.

**Live to thrive** – Awareness campaign about drink & drive, **Amar Jawan** – Providing Financial assistance to the needy families of the Martyrs, **Lead the Blind** – Helping the blind students, **Save the Wild** – Campaign to save the endangered animals & adopting animals in Zoos, are some of the social responsibility themes adopt by the college during its Annual Fest celebration over last few years. Apart from this ATME Colle of Engineering has adopted a Govt. School in Melanahalli and provided basic amenities and Infrastructure to the School along with free Computer training and awareness in Modern Technology for their Students.

To promote the talent students the ATMECE has come up with a scheme called “Vidyaasare” in which the meritorious students of PUC / CET will be given free education including free transportation under Management Quota. Around Rs.60.0 lakh of Scholarship has given for more than 50 talented students since 2018.

## NVH Technology and CNC Technology

Department of mechanical engineering is organized a webinar on the topic **NVH Technology and CNC Technology** **on 5** **th** **Aug 2021** for the  benefit of students. This webinar conducted in association with **Govt. Tool** **Room and Training Centre, Mysore, Mr. Praveen V and Mr. Pavan** **Kumar N,** speakers of this webinar explained the on the above said topics. Prof.  Devaraj M R welcomed all the faculty and student participants for this program. The webinar started at 3.00 PM and finished at 4.30 PM after the discussions  and interactions for the participants queries. Mr. Praveen V the speaker of the  webinar started his speech and briefed on Noise, Vibration and Harshness and  its sources.

The speaker Mr. Pavan Kumar N spoke on CNC Technology and also  various training programs providing at GTTC to the students. The session was  completed after expressing thanks to speakers and all participants by Dr.  Srinivasa K.

The team involved in organizing this event are **Dr. Rathnakar G** Prof.  and Dean, and **Dr. Srinivasa K** HOD, Department of Mechanical Engineering,  as convenors. The program coordinated by **Prof. Devaraj M R, Dr.** **Mohanakumara K C** and **Prof. Niranjan kumar V S** Department of  Mechanical Engineering.

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/20.jpg)

Hybrid Electrical Vehicle Technology- Basics

Department of mechanical engineering is organized a webinar on the topic Hybrid Electrical Vehicle- Basics on 28th July 2021 for the benefit of students. This webinar conducted in association with Toyota Kirloskar Motors Ltd. Bidadi, Bangalore. Mr. Ashwin D Souza, speaker of this webinar explained the basics on the above said topic. Prof. Devaraj M R welcomed all the faculty and student participants for this program. The webinar started at 3.30 PM and finished at 5.15 P M after the discussions and interactions for the participants queries. Mr. Ashwin D Souza the presenter of the webinar started his speech and briefed right from the history of automobiles and their revolutions as the technology developed.

In his speech highlighted on categories of xEV vehicles such as Battery EV, Fuel Cell EV and Hybrid EV etc. He also touched upon the hybrid variants such as Micro, Mild and Strong.

The speaker also spoke on Batteries like Lead-Acid battery, Lithium-Ion battery and solid-state battery. Mr. Ashwin also covered about function of Electric motor and power control unit in the hybrid vehicles including upcoming technologies in the field of automotive sector. The session was completed after expressing thanks to speaker and all participants by Dr. Srinivasa K.

The team involved in organizing this event are Dr. Rathnakar G Prof. and Dean, Dr. Srinivasa K HOD, Department of Mechanical Engineering. The program coordinated by Prof. Devaraj M R, Dr. Mohanakumara K C and Prof. Niranjan kumar V S Department of Mechanical Engineering.

## Report on IICDC Contest

**About IICDC:**

Texas Instruments in collaboration with Department of Science and Technology (DST), powered by AICTE mission proudly announce the DST & Texas Instruments India Innovation Challenge Design Contest 2019 anchored by NSRCEL, Indian Institute of Management, Bangalore (IIMB) and supported by MyGov. The contest is open for all Indian engineering students pursuing undergraduate, postgraduate &Doctoral degrees with Indian engineering colleges.

Texas Instruments (TI) invites all student innovators, thinkers and makers of the country to join the revolution, who have a dream to create something new, aspire to make a difference, contribute to India’s success towards becoming an Innovation Hub.

**Team ID:** **1392433**

## Department of Science & Technology (DST)

**Department of Science and Technology (DST)**, Science for Equity Empowerment and Development (SEED) Division, **Government of India,** has sanctioned an amount of **Rs. 2.05Cr(Two crore rupees)** to implement the project titled **“Innovative ICT Enabled Co-Working Community Center Design for Rural Development”**.

The proposed project will be established at **ATME College of Engineering Mysuru.** Through this project it is proposed to empower the youths belonging to scheduled caste (SC) and scheduled tribe communities (ST) through the application of science technology and innovations (STI) hubs. The project aims at empowering the youths by providing co working community center.

The principal investigator of this project is Dr.Mahesh.P.K, professor and head Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering, ATME College of Engineering Mysuru and Co-Investigator is Dr.Prakashkuravatti, Associate professor, Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering, ATME College of Engineering Mysuru.

The proposed project aims to increase the livelihood of the rural masses and also enhance the socioeconomic status of people of Mysore and nearby vicinity.The project provides innovative solutions for the community living on five **STERM** forces, namely **Science** research that generates new and or improved products, New emerging **Technologies**, New **Engineering** materials and designs from Government and Social Institutions in service chains, **Regulations** and policies with regard to infrastructure, trade, New **Management** techniques and business models such as out sourcing, sell direct, supply hubs, e-retail, telemedicine, are invented to enable growth.Through this project **ATMECollege of Engineering** will provide a technology enabled community space which is accessible to the local community of the region.

This proposed facility is intended to be internet enabled and will allow 24\*7 accesses to the targeted beneficiaries. This STI Hub will be Technology enabled community center & will ensure sustainable rural livelihood promotion in tune to the particular societal requirements.

In addition to the above,facilities like room for cold storage, community-based skill development through online / offline mentoring, room for developing prototypes – translation of idea to products will be facilitated. The STI Hub will be a facility for the villagers to become technologically self-sufficient and solve the local community problems using the tools available in the Maker’sSpace.

The STI Hub will focus on the following streams of training like Advanced Sewing Machine Training Program, Skill Development Programme, Up-Skill Development programme, Training Program for Agri/Electronic Kit -to test/analyze/repair/fix and Resolve community problems. The overall objective of implementing this project is for the overall up liftment of the rural youth and society at large.

“Honorable chairman of ATME College of Engineering **Sri L.Arunkumar**, and members of **management** have appreciated and congratulated the effort of members involved in executing the said DST project. Further the management of ATMECE is committed to provide required support   to execute this project as per DST guide lines for the benefit of rural population”.

[DST Project Sanctioned  – Report](/__l5e/assets-v1/1c6484f4-1d05-4ee9-831c-4b16f5408c2d/DST-Report.pdf)

## International Women’s Day celebration – 2021

**Details of Chief Guest and Guest of Honour for International Women’s Day 2021**

**_Chief Guest_**

**Dr. Shalini Nalwad**

Chairperson ICATT Foundation

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/women1-300x200-1.jpg)

Dr. Shalini Nalwad graduated from Mysore University and obtained her Fellowship in Anaesthesia from the College of Anaesthetist, Ireland. She also has a Membership from the Royal College of Anaesthetist, UK. She secured the prestigious medical training programme of The Northern Ireland, Deanery. During her tenure as a trainee in a medical rotation, she led the Cardiac Arrest Team, the Mobile Cardiac ICU and has lysed the patients in the community, and successfully resuscitated cardiac arrests in the community.

She has gained extensive experience working in the Tertiary Intensive Care Unit in Belfast for three years which mainly deals with trauma. She is associated with Europe’s leading Air ambulance company and has transferred Level 2 to Level 3 patients across the world. She was able to retrieve patients from 5 countries, 2 continents in 72 hours and has undeterringly airlifted patients from Libya in midst of the turmoil. She was also part of the Panel at the 6th Annual Conference of Indian College of Anaesthesiologists in collaboration with University of Minnesota, USA, Nov 2014.

Dr. Nalwad is an ECMO specialist from Leicester Glenfield Hospital UK, (June 2015) and will be launching the first ever Airborne ECMO in India. Realising the gaps in Indian medical system she, along with others have associated to form ICATT, which can help make the emergency medical transfer a reality in India and also make it affordable to the needy.

**_Guest of Honor_**

**Mrs. Nandini Murthy**

Nutritionist and Wellness Consultant

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/women2.jpg)

Mrs. Nandini Murthy is a leading consultant Nutritionist with a long-standing career in VLCC in Hospitals and Clinics in Bangalore and Mysore. She was into teaching, and some of her nutrition-related articles have been published in leading newspapers. With an experience of more than 20 years, she realized that many patients with diabetes from all walks of life including the highly educated are not entirely aware of diabetes.

She has been spreading awareness by delivering talks on obesity and wellness. She offers therapeutic counseling for patients such as corporate professionals and school children. She worked as a Patient educator in her earlier stint.  Mrs. Murthy is certified and trained in Acupressure, Acutouch, Magnetic therapy, Auricular therapy, Mudras, Meditation and Yoga.

## TALK ON “GENDER JUSTICE: LAW ON HINDU WOMEN PROPERTY RIGHT”

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/9001-01.jpg)

The College Internal Complaint Committee (CICC), ATME College of Engineering (ATMECE), Mysuru in association with All India Women Conference (AIWC) had organized a One Day Talk on **“Gender Justice: Law on Hindu Women Property Right” recently, to cr** eate awareness among the students about evolution of laws of succession to women’s property, if any property possessed by a female Hindu. The objective of the talk is to discuss holistically about the concurrent issues on Gender Equality and Women Property Rights.

The Resource person, **Dr. Janhavi S S, Dept. of studies in law KSOU Mysuru** addressed the gathering and introduced about the Hindu Succession Act 1956 and some of the keywords such as coparcener, Mitakshara, Dayabhaga, ancestral property, separate property, self acquired property etc explained about the evolution of the Women’s Property Rights over the decades and Amendments taken place since from 1956 till recent times. During the session, She gave a clear insight on Gender Justice from the Perspective of Hindu Woman’s Property Right, Right to Equality, concept of Survivorship & succession, Widow’s Estate, Social justice and also about the Court Cases – wherein the landmark decisions gave from the Supreme Court about equal coparcenary rights by birth for the Women  as per the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005.

**The Chief Guest Mrs. Ashitha S, National Vice President AIWC, New Delhi** joined Online to the Program and during the speech, introduced about the establishment of All India Women’s Conference (AIWC) and about its key initiatives taken at various capacities and appreciated ATMECE for taking initiative for conducting a program on Gender Justice and Woman Property Rights apart from the Technical Aspect conferences.

Further, **The Guest of Honor Mrs. Hemalatha M A, Executive Council Member, AIWC, Advocate and Notary** addressed the gathering and motivated youth to know their Rights and responsibilities especially Voting Rights and their role in shaping the future, as she mentioned that today’s younger generation youths are the Tomorrow’s Nation builders.

**Dr. L Basavaraj, Principal, ATMECE** presided over the function and gave a Presidential Speech stating that the Gender Equality is the Human Right and appreciated the AICW for associating with CICC-ATMECE for the initiative taken to create awareness through the one-day program. And also mentioned that, the Program is going to be more beneficial and useful for all.

**Dr. Bhagyashree S R, Chairperson CICC, Prof & Dean- Research, ATMECE,** addressed the gathering and Thanked AIWC Vice President and other members of the committee for associating with CICC to organize the Program. During the speech, commemorated the dignity of the Woman and Woman Empowerment in Ancient Civilization and Equal status of Woman in Early Vedic period and expressed concerns of diminishing the Woman Rights over the last 3 Centuries. Also introduced about the establishment of CICC at ATME inline with regulations received from Visvesvaraya Technological University, Belagavi and introduced about the various initiatives taken by the CICC in creating awareness among the students w.r.t Natural Rights, Social Justice etc.

In the valedictory session, Online Speakers, Resources Persons, other AIWC Mysuru branch members Program Convener Dr. Bhagyashree S R, Faculty Coordinators and Technical staff were present.

## Talk on “Career Opportunities in the IC Design Industry”

**Organizing Department Name:** ECE

**Title of the event: Talk on “Career Opportunities in the IC Design Industry”**

**Date: 26** **th** **April 2021**

**Venue: ATME College of Engineering**

**Resource person/Guest:**

Sunil Kumar H V, Designated Partner,

https://www.linkedin.com/in/sunil-kumar-hv-0b103415/

Audience: 6th and 4th Semester students of ATMECE, Mysore

**Brief Description about the event:**  The objective of this talk is to introduce undergraduate students to the various opportunities in the VLSI industry. The IC Design industry offers the largest number of employment opportunities to undergraduates from Electronics based branches. Proper preparation from the student’s parts can make them employable in the IC Design Industry. Therefore, opening up a dearth of opportunities for the students. The talk will provide students an overview of the industry from Mr. Sunil Kumar, who has been in the IC Industry since past 15+ years in Industry. He has worked in various roles as Engineer, Building Teams Across Domains in VLSI, in Leadership & Management, in Sales & Marketing, in Finance. It is a very good opportunity for students to learn and collect information from a Professional of the IC Industry.

## Report on Induction Program 2020-2021

**Report**

on

**Induction Program 2020-2021**

The induction program for the first-year admitted students for the academic year 2020-2021 was conducted from 21/12/2020 to 29/12/2020. Various events, talk from eminent personalities were organized throughout this program. The induction program was conducted online mode through the Microsoft Teams platform.

The induction program for newly admitted students was conducted in line with the AICTE Induction program policy. The induction program will be conducted every year before the commencement of the first semester classes as per VTU guidelines by the trained faculties.

The objective of the Induction program was to demystify the expectation of the students from the Intermediate level and to provide an adequate foundation in the Applied Science subjects and English Which is limited to a moderate level so that students do not face any problems when the regular class commences.

The SIP was planned to keep in view the overall personality development which includes soft skills, sports, and Cultural Activities. The duration of the induction program was THREE weeks. The students were given insights about Universal Human Values apart from other co-curricular and extra-curricular activities. During this program, the students will come out of their hesitation and it will be the best platform for the students to interact with the faculty members and to build strong relationships with them.

This Student Induction Programme (SIP) was also conducted for the last two years for our students. It was observed that there was a gradual improvement in the overall performance of the students. Their parents have also deeply appreciated it. This induction program will help the students to have a smooth transition to the Engineering course.

**Objectives of SIP:**

- Make the students feel comfortable in the new environment.
- Allow them to explore their academic interests and activities.
- Reduce competition and make them work for excellence.
- Build a strong relationship between teachers and students.
- Give a broader view of life.
- Build a Character.

At the start of the induction, the incumbents learn about the institutional policies, processes, practices, culture, and values, familiarization to the respective branch/stream.

In the Orientation Program on Day 1, the Principal, Deans, and other college functionaries addressed and welcome the new students along with their parents. It served to provide space for telling the new students about the college, and their academic and student life.

The details of various events that were conducted in the induction program are as follows.

**Day 1:** **12/21/2020**

**Inauguration Session:**

**Dr.Basavaraj. L**, Principal ATME College of Engineering welcomed all the fresh students who were admitted to ATME College of Engineering for the academic year 2020-2021, Principal also welcomed  Parents, Deans, HoD’s, and all the staff’s on this occasion.

Further principal briefed the students about the college facilities, infrastructure, and the organizational structure and organizational hierarchy.

**Sri. L. Arun Kumar** Honourable Chairman, ATME College of Engineering, addressed the students and advised the students not to relax after joining the Engineering program and to work hard to achieve higher heights.

**Dr. Govinde Gowda M S**, Dean Academics, briefed the students about the VTU Norms & Regulations.

**Dr. Rathnakar G**, Dean Student Affairs, briefed the students about the services from the office of Dean Student Affairs. Further, he briefed about the facilities like scholarship, extracurricular activities, NSS activities, etc.,

**Dr. Mahesh Lohith K S**, Associate Professor & HOD, Physics Department briefed the students about the importance of **“Counselling & Mentoring”** and informed the students about the measures initiated by the college to prevent ragging.

**Dr. Bhagyashree S R,** Dean Research and chairman College internal complaint committee **(CICC)** briefed the students about the significance and function of CICC.

**Mr. Kiran B,** Assistant professor Department of Computer science briefed about the use of College Enterprise Resource Planning (CERP) to the students.

**Day 2:** **12/22/2020**

**Mr.Thejkumar J**, Assistant professor Department of Mechanical Engineering, conducted a session on Universal Human Value (UHV) on the topic **“Purpose of the course, Student Aspiration, Family Expectation, Gratitude”.**

**Dr. Srinivasa K** Professor and Head, Department of Mechanical Engineering, addressed the students and shared information about the facilities available in the ME department and the various initiatives taken in the department.

**Mr.Vinod Prabhu**, Managing Director-Seventh Sense Talent Solutions, addressed the students and emphasized the **” importance of training to prepare for interviews and ways to clear interviews”.**

**Dr.Avinash K**, Assistant Professor, Dept. of Chemistry, engaged awareness session about COVID-19 precautions and preventive measures at ATMECE.

**Day 3: 12/23/2020**

**Ms.Bharathi R** Assistant professor Department of humanities conducted a session on Universal Human Value (UHV) on the topic **“Competition and Cooperation, Competition and Excellence”.**

**Dr. Parthasarathy**, Professor, and Head, Department of Electrical & Electronics Engineering, addressed the students and shared information about the facilities available in the EEE department and the various initiatives taken in the department.

**Dr.Raghavendra Prasad M D**, Founder & Managing Director, M/S. RPV Engineering Consultants Pvt Ltd. addressed the students and emphasized the role of **“Engineers in Innovation & Entrepreneurship”.**

**Dr.Aditya R**. **Nakade,** Consultant Ophthalmologist & Vitreo Retinal Surgeon Agarwal eye Hospital, Mysore, delivered a session on “ **Protection of eyes against the use of electronic gadgets”.**

**Day 4:** **12/24/2020**

**Dr.Chethan S**, Assistant professor Department of Mechanical Engineering, conducted a session on Universal Human Value (UHV) on the topic **“Peer Pressure and ways to handle peer pressure”.**

**Mr. Manu Vijay** Associate professor and Head, Department of Civil engineering, addressed the students and shared the information about the facilities available in the Civil engineering department and the various initiatives taken in the department.

**Dr.T S Sathyanarayana Rao,** Professor JSS medical college, Honorary General Secretary, Indian Psychiatric Society, delivered a lecture on **“Stress Management and Adolescent problems”.**

**Sri. Gajanana Londhe**,  Executive Director, Samvit Research Foundation, Head of Strategy & Transformation at Nokia, Bangalore delivered a session on “ **National Education Policy    NEP-2020 Overview & Opportunities.”**

**Day 5:** **12/28/2020**

**Mrs.Priyanka N B,** Assistant professor Department of Mathematics, conducted a session on Universal Human Value (UHV) on the topic **“Self and Body(Session-1)”.**

**Dr. Mahesh P K** Professor and Head, Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering, addressed the students and shared information about the facilities available in the ECE department and the various initiatives taken in the department.

**Sri. Sharath Chandra,** Manager-Devices, Reliance Jio Infocom Limited, Bangalore delivered a session on **“Recent trends and challenges in engineering”.**

**Mr.Thungaraju G D,** Co-Founder of People Mechanics and Founder of TIECEE, delivered a session on **“Innovation & Entrepreneurship”**

**Day 6:** **12/29/2020**

**Mr.Ramachandra N,** Assistant professor Department of physics conducted a session on Universal Human Value (UHV) on the topic **“Self and Body (Session-2)”.**

**Dr.Kalpana Gopalan,** IAS, PhD-IIMB, Additional Chief Secretary Department Of Youth Empowerment & Sports, delivered a lecture session on **“NEP’s focus on Governance, Leadership, innovation, Entrepreneurship in Higher Education”.**

**Dr. Putte Gowda,** Professor & Head, Department of Computer science & Engineering, addressed the students and shared information about the facilities available in the CSE department and the various initiatives taken in the department.

The last session was on Creative Arts and in this session, students showcased their various talents in extracurricular and cultural activities.

The program was concluded with a valedictory session by Dr. Rathnakar G., Dean-Student Affairs proposed the Vote of Thanks and thanked the Management, Principal, Deans, HODs and students and all those who contributed to the success of the induction program

## OBESERVATION OF “NATIONAL VOTERS DAY-2020-21” AT ATME

ATME College of engineering, Bannur Road Mysuru, had organized online quiz and essay competition to the students in view of observing “National Voters Day-2020-21” and to create awareness about electoral process in prospective voters of India, as per the directives of State Chief Election Commission and Visvesvaraya Technological University- Belagavi.

On the occasion, an Online Essay Competition as well as Quiz was organized. The Topic of Essay was “ **The Importance of Free and Fare Regular Elections in India**”. More than 36 students had participated in the event and top 3 students selected were recommended for higher level.

The response for Quiz was overwhelming more than 115 students participating in the event. Top 3 students selected were recommended for district level competition.

The event was coordinated by Mr. Chandrashekar C. Lecturer Department of Basic Science & Humanities, under the guidance of Dr. L. Basavaraj, Principal and Dr. Rathnakar. G. Dean Student Affairs, ATMECE.

The top three students from the district level competition will be eligible to compete at State level. The competition has attractive prizes to the winners.

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/69.jpg)

## Workshop on Database Application Development

**Organizing Department Name**:  Department of Computer Science & Engineering.

**Event type:** Within department.

**Title of the event**: Workshop on Database Application Development

**Date**: 23/12/2020 and 24/12/2020

**Venue**: Department of Computer Science & Engineering, ATMECE.

**Resource person/Guest: Name:** Mr Anil Kumar and Mrs Rashmi K,

**Designation:** Assistant Professor

**Event Description**: Conducting two days of workshop on “Database Application Development” in CS Dept. This workshop is targeted to pre final year students for implementation of mini project using database.

This workshop concentrated on different front end design tool like PHP, JAVA and JSP with MySql database.

Day 1: Will be takeover by Resource person Mrs Rashmi K concentrating on following topics

- Installation of JAVA
- Java Database Connectivity process
- Java Server Pages.
- Creating database and table in MySQL.
- Implementing simple application using JSP with MySQL.
- Insert new record, update record and delete record operation in application.
- Applying Triggers and stored procedure to application.

Day 2: Will be takeover by Resource person Mr Anil Kumar concentrating

- Introduction to PHP
- Syntax and defining rule for PHP
- Installation and description of XAMPP tool.
- Simple Login page implementation using database.
- Insert, update and delete operation on application.
- Applying Triggers and stored procedure to application.

### **ATMEYA 2K26**

#### 📅 10 – 11 April 2026 \| 📍 ATME College of Engineering

#### ABOUT ATMEYA – 2K26 THEME

**HONOR THE HANDS THAT KEEP OUR CITY CLEAN – PAURA KARMIKARU**

The Annual Cultural Fest ATMEYA 2K26 of ATME College of Engineering will th th be celebrated on 10 and 11 April 2026 with the meaningful theme “Honor the Hands that Keep Our City Clean.” This theme highlights the impoance of recognizing and appreciating the invaluable contributions of sanitation workers who tirelessly work to maintain cleanliness, hygiene and public health in our city. The fest aims to instill a sense of social responsibility, gratitude and respect among students by acknowledging the dedication and hard work of those who oen remain unnoticed in society. Through various cultural programs, awareness activities and student-led initiatives, the event will emphasize the dignity of labor and the impoance of community paicipation in keeping our surroundings clean and sustainable.

ATMEYA 2K26 will also serve as a vibrant plaorm for students to showcase their creativity, talent and teamwork through competitions, peormances and interactive events. By aligning celebration with social awareness, the fest aspires to inspire students to contribute positively to society while honoring the real heroes who keep our city clean every day.

02. The Graduands are requested to assemble in the Auditorium before 9:15 AM on 24-01-2026.

03. The Graduands are requested to occupy their reserved seat only.

04. Clapping hands/Whistling/Eatables/Chewing gums are strictly prohibited.

05. The Graduands are not allowed inside the auditorium after the commencement of ceremony

06. Please stand up when the academic procession enters the Auditorium and remain standing till the members of the procession take their seats.

07. Graduands are requested to take the pledge audibly after initiation by the Chairman.

08. Graduands are also requested to stay back in their seats, after receiving the certificate till the end of the Session.

09. At the closing of the ceremony, please remain standing till the academic procession leaves.

10. Mobile phones/Cameras are strictly not allowed inside the auditorium.

11. It is a solemn ceremony; silence is solicited throughout the programme.

12. Parents/Guardians are requested to occupy their reserved seats only.

### **FIVE-DAY FDP on “Real-Time Digital Signal Processing & Generative AI in Multimodal Medical Imaging”**

#### Date: 6th to 10th January 2026

**ABOUT THE FDP**

The FDP on Real-Time Digital Signal Processing and Generative AI in Multimodal Medical Imaging is planned to give VTU and other faculty members a comprehensive understanding of advanced DSP and AI concepts with applications in healthcare, aligning with curriculum requirements and supporting teaching, research and interdisciplinary work.

**OBJECTIVES OF FDP**

• Enhance understanding of real-time DSP concepts and applications.

• Introduce generative AI techniques for multimodal medical imaging.

• Provide hands-on exposure to DSP tools, algorithms and hardware.

• Familiarise the participants with digital pathology, CT scanning and multimodal Gen AI transformer modelling

### **DATUM 2k25 – State-Level Technical Fest by the Department of Civil Engineering**

The Department of Civil Engineering proudly presents “DATUM 2K25”, a premier state-level technical fest organized annually since 2017. Over the years, DATUM has evolved into a vibrant platform that celebrates innovation, knowledge sharing, and the spirit of healthy competition among budding Civil Engineering Students.

The fest was conceived with a vision to foster a positive and engaging learning environment, encouraging students to explore their technical potential while nurturing creativity, teamwork, and leadership skills. It serves as a dynamic forum where participants gain hands-on exposure, build confidence, and develop essential professional skills in an inspiring atmosphere.

Each year, students from across the state with a civil engineering background enthusiastically participate in DATUM, making it a wonderful platform to showcase talent, exchange knowledge, and experience learning through fun.

#### **Date: 29th October 2025**

**Technical Events**

**\> CAD-Do –** Test your design speed and accuracy in this “fastest fingers in CAD drawing” challenge.

**\> Quizzie –** Sharpen your civil engineering intellect through a competitive and fun-filled quiz.

**\> Poster Presentation –** Showcase your innovative ideas and research through creative poster displays.

**\> Waste Wizard (Ideathon) –** Present sustainable and practical solutions to real-world waste management challenges.

**Non-Technical Events**

**\> Minute Mania –** Engage in exciting one-minute games that blend wit, agility, and fun.

**\> Reels Fun –** Express your creativity and storytelling skills through short, engaging videos.

Through its blend of technical rigor and creative expression, DATUM continues to inspire students to learn, compete, and connect — transforming classroom learning into real-world innovation.

**Registration Link:**

[https://forms.gle/GTGxaF6BxUutodkU9](https://forms.gle/GTGxaF6BxUutodkU9)

**Rules and Regulations**

**Title of the event: Poster presentation**

– Theme: Sustainable practices in civil engineering

– Two in a team

– Poster size: 27” (width) x40” (height)

– Presentation time: Maximum 4 minutes

– Participants should bringtheir own printed posters and place it at their designated stand specified at the event venue

**Title of the event: Wizard Event- Ideathon**

– Students must register for the event on or before 28.10.2025.

– Each team can have a maximum of two participants.

– All submissions and ideas must be original, innovative, and practical.

– Entries will be evaluated based on problem understanding, innovation, feasibility, and impact.

– The best idea will be selected for presentation at the venue, and the top two teams will receive Cash prizes.

**Title of the event: Quizziee**

– Two in a team

– Entry Fee: 50 per person

– First round: MCQ

– Second round : Oral ( 6 teams)

– judges’ decision will be final

**Title of the event: Cad Do**

– Solo Participant

– Entry fee: 50

– First round : MCQ

– Second round : Drawing ( single line diagram will provided, Plan and elevation shall be drawn by Participant)

– Evaluation will be based on Accuracy, Precision, Completion , drafting

– judges’ decision will be final

[![ATME College of Engineering](/__l5e/assets-v1/4519b204-1c5c-4570-ad02-6e238e674849/ATME-Final-logo-copy.png)](/p/)

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/grad-1200x600.jpg)

- June 28, 2025
- Mysuru,Karnataka

### Graduation Day – 2025

**Greetings from ATME College of Engineering, Mysuru !!!**

Graduation Day marks a **major milestone** in a student’s life, symbolizing the successful completion of an academic journey and the beginning of a new chapter. Its significance extends beyond just receiving a certificate or degree — it embodies growth, transformation, and future responsibility.

We are delighted to inform you that the Graduation Day – 2025 of ATME College of Engineering, Mysuru is scheduled to be held on **Saturday, 28th June 2025 at 9:30 AM in the College Auditorium.**

We take immense pleasure in inviting you to grace the occasion with your esteemed presence and encourage the graduating students as they embark on a new journey of their lives.

Your presence will add glory to the event and inspire our students as they receive their graduation certificates in the august presence of distinguished guests and academic leaders.

**Information to the Graduands:**

The ceremony will be held in two sessions.

**SESSION-1:**

- Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE), Computer Science and Design (CSD), Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning (AIML) Graduands will occupy the reserved seats in the auditorium by **9.15AM.**
- Electrical and Electronics Engineering (EEE) Graduands will be stationed in the auditorium throughout the ceremony and shall occupy the reserved seats by **9.15AM.**
- Computer Science & Engineering (CSE) Graduands will occupy Room No. AB205 & AB206 in Admin block by **9.15AM.**
- Data Science (DS) Graduands will occupy Room No. AB207 in Admin block by **9.15AM.**
- Civil Engineering (CV) and Mechanical Engineering (ME) Graduands will occupy Room No. AB208 in Admin block by **9.15AM.**

**SESSION-2:**

After completion of Graduation Day-2025 ceremony Session-1,

- CV, DS, ME and CSE Graduands will occupy the reserved seats in the auditorium.
- ECE Graduands will occupy Room No. AB205 & 206 in Admin block.
- AIML Graduands will occupy Room No. AB207 in Admin block.
- CSD Graduands will occupy Room No. AB208 in Admin block.

**Note:** Graduands will receive guidance from their respective department coordinators

**Instructions to the Graduands**

01. The Graduands should report to the campus and collect the stole and reserved seat no. from the department coordinators before **8.45AM**.
02. The Graduands are informed to assemble in the Auditorium (wear only informed attire, Boys: Full sleeves white shirt, Black Trousers, Black Belt, Formal Shoes: Black, Girls: Cream (Off-White) Onam Saree with Golden Colour Blouse) before **9:15 AM**.
03. Graduands may bring a maximum of two accompanying guests. Seating for Accompanying guests is arranged in Room No. AB401, and they are required to be seated before 9:45 AM. Arrangements have been made to livestream the Graduation Day ceremony in Room No. AB401 for their viewing.
04. Mobile phones/cameras are strictly not allowed inside the auditorium.
05. The Graduands are informed to occupy their reserved seat only.
06. The Graduands are informed to maintain the dignity of the Graduation ceremony.
07. It is a solemn ceremony; silence is solicited throughout the programme.
08. Clapping hands/ Whistling/ Eatables/Chewing gums are strictly prohibited.
09. The Graduands are not allowed inside the auditorium after the commencement of ceremony.
10. The Graduands are informed to stand up when the academic procession enters the hall and remain standing till the members of the procession occupy their seats.
11. Graduands should remain standing during the play of Naadageethe at the beginning and National Anthem at the end of the ceremony.
12. Graduands should receive certificate respectfully with both hands and also acknowledge saying ‘Thanks’.
13. The Graduands are informed to take the Oath audibly in the standing position after initiated by the Dignitary
14. The Graduands should stay back in their reserved seat, after receiving the certificate.
15. At the closing of the ceremony, Graduands should remain standing till the academic procession leaves.
16. Group Photo Session will be held in the order given below after the completion of Graduation ceremony:

      1\. ECE  2. CSD 3. AIML 4. CSE 5. DS   6. CV     7. EEE   8. ME
17. Graduands are cordially invited to have lunch (at Cafeteria Ground floor) with accompanying guests (at Boys Common Area- Admin Block).
18. Graduands shall take part in the photo session first and later proceed to have lunch.
19. Accompanying guests, who are unable to visit campus for the Graduation Day ceremony can witness the event through online via YouTube live @ ATMECE Official channel.
20. Car parking facility for Accompanying guests is at college football playground.

**Note:**

1. Graduands registration and seating: before 9.15AM
2. Accompanying guests seating: before 9.45AM
3. Graduation Day-2025 ceremony: 9.45AM to 1PM
4. Photo Session: 1PM – 1:30PM
5. Lunch for Accompanying guests: 1:30PM Onwards
6. Lunch for Graduands: After department photo session

### “INDIAN KNOWLEDGE SYSTEM”

#### **Date**

#### **5th – 7th March 2025**

### About Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS)

The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 emphasizes integrating Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) into STEM, engineering, and technical education. It promotes multidisciplinary learning, drawing from India’s heritage in science, mathematics, architecture, metallurgy, and sustainability. Engineering & Technical Institutions are incorporating Vedic mathematics, Ayurveda-based biotechnology, and temple architecture into curricula. NEP also encourages research in Sanskrit texts, indigenous technologies, and traditional craftsmanship to foster innovation. By blending modern advancements with India’s intellectual traditions, this approach strengthens STEM education, ensuring a globally competitive, culturally rooted learning ecosystem.

### About FDP

Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) (Bhāratīya-JñānaParampara) encompasses the treasure of knowledge in various disciplines that emerged systematically from the ancient times in India over generations. IKS as a theme and topic of interest has emerged as one of the important components of Contemporary Education. It is one of the “verticals” under NEP-2020 in Higher Education in India. The upside of this is the vast literature (predominantly in vernacular media), practices and artifacts available related to IKS. The downside of this is a diametrically opposite situation concerning IKS as related to the STEM domain. It is here that Engineering and Technical Education has been on the backfoot, Unable to address issues of concern in IKS from a STEM point of view.

This Three-Day Faculty Development Program (FDP) focuses on cybersecurity awareness and the role of emerging technologies—Blockchain, Artificial Intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), and Quantum Computing—in securing social media and banking applications. The program will feature expert-led sessions, hands-on discussions, and case studies to equip participants with advanced knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks, risk mitigation strategies, and secure system implementations. ### THREE DAYS FDP ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, MACHINE LEARNING & DEEP LEARNING IN THE DATA REVOLUTION ERA: PROGRESS & APPLICATIONS

### Organized by   Department of Computer Science & Engineering   and Department of CSE-AIML

**Date :****3rd February to 5th February 2025**

**Venue**

**ATME College of Engineering**

**0821-2954081 \| 0821 -2954011**

**[Info@atme.edu.in](mailto:Info@atme.edu.in) \| [www.atme.edu.in](/p/)**

**13th Kilometer, Mysore – Kanakapura – Bangalore Road,**

**Mysore – 570 028**

### About FDP

The aim of this Faculty Development Program (FDP) is to enrich participants’ understanding of the latest advancements in AI, ML, and DL, along with their emerging applications. Esteemed experts from prestigious academic institutions and leading industries will be invited to share their insights and experiences in research. This FDP is designed to inspire beginners to cultivate an interest in AI, ML, and DL, while also supporting researchers in advancing their work in these domains.

### **About Student Induction Program**

A **Student Induction Program** (SIP) is an orientation initiative for new students, particularly in higher education institutions like universities and colleges. The goal of the SIP is to help students transition smoothly into their new academic environment, foster a sense of belonging, and provide them with the necessary tools to succeed both academically and personally.

The **Student Induction Program** in educational institutions is an initiative implemented under the guidelines of the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) and followed by Visvesvaraya Technological University (VTU). It is designed to help students transition into engineering education and acclimate to the college environment while fostering their holistic development.

### **Key Objectives**

The primary goals of the **AICTE and VTU** mandated **Student Induction Program** are to:

1. **Acclimatize students to the new academic environment:** Help students adjust to the university’s academic and social environment.
2. **Bridge the gap between school and professional education:** Introduce students to engineering education and its demands, equipping them with necessary skills for academic success.
3. **Build soft skills and ethics:** Foster values like teamwork, communication, leadership, and ethics.
4. **Promote physical and emotional well-being:** Engage students in activities related to physical fitness, emotional stability, and mental health.
5. **Encourage social responsibility:** Instill a sense of responsibility and promote engagement with society through community service or projects.

### **Program Structure**

The induction program typically lasts for three weeks and includes a variety of activities divided into five main areas:

1. **Physical Activity:**
   - Regular exercises, yoga sessions, and sports activities to promote physical health.
   - Developing discipline and a healthy lifestyle.
2. **Mentoring Sessions:**
   - Senior students, faculty, or external mentors guide new students, helping them adjust to college life.
   - Discussions on values, ethics, and dealing with stress.
3. **Universal Human Values (UHV):**
   - Workshops on universal human values focus on self-reflection, building good relationships, and understanding the importance of ethics and social responsibility.
   - Encourages students to think about their role in society and their responsibilities as future professionals.
4. **Creative Arts and Culture:**
   - Engagement in creative activities like painting, music, dance, and other arts to enhance creativity and self-expression.
   - Exposure to Indian culture and heritage.
5. **Literary and Proficiency Modules:**
   - Sessions to improve communication skills, especially in English, along with team-building exercises.
   - Workshops on life skills, goal setting, and time management.
6. **Awareness Sessions :**

- Sessions to create awareness on Cyber Crime, Social Responsibilities and  Health Foundations.

### **Power Electronics Applications in Medical Electronics**

The Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering under Department Association Quantum is organizing a Technical Talk on “Power Electronics Applications in Medical Electronics” for IV and VI Semester Students of EEE.

**Event Date :22.07.2024**

**Event Time:10.30AM to 12Noon**

**Venue:EE004**

### **Resource Person: Mr. Srinivas N R**

**Senior Power Electronics Engineer**

**GE Healthcare, Bengaluru**

**Objectives of the Technical Talk:**

**Objective 1:** Understand the Role of Power Electronics in Medical Devices

To provide a comprehensive understanding of how power electronics is applied in the design and functionality of various medical devices, such as X Ray, MRI machines, pacemakers, and diagnostic equipment.

**Objective 2:** Explore Advanced Power Electronics Technologies and Their Applications, Impact on Healthcare

To explore advanced power electronics technologies, including DC-DC converters, inverters, and power management systems, and their impact on enhancing the performance, efficiency, and reliability of medical electronics.

**Objective 3:** Highlight Potential Job Prospects in Power Electronics and Medical   Electronics

To highlight potential career opportunities and job prospects in the field of power electronics and medical electronics, guiding students on the skills and qualifications needed to pursue these careers.

**Expected Outcomes of the Technical Talk:**

**The students will be able to:**

**Outcome-1:** Apply Power Electronics Principles in Medical Device Design

**Outcome-2:** Outline Knowledge of Power Electronics, Signals & Systems, High Voltage Engineering in Medical Applications

**Outcome-3:** Infer the Career Opportunities and Industry Requirements.

### Report on Annual Cultural fest ATMEya-2k25

**“Ability beyond disability”**

ATMEya is the annual college cultural fest that ATME has been organizing since the Inception of this college from 2010. The students, staff and Management of this institution have repeatedly established standards which have been constantly beaten in the consecutive years. ATMEya has been based on a wide array of themes – from Traffic Awareness, Amar Jawan to Lead the Blind and Arise-Awake-Adopt  Orphans. This year ATMEya is based on the theme “Ability beyond disability” held on 23rd and 24th May 2025.

### REPORT ON TECHAVISHKAR 2.0 24-HOUR   HACKATHON CONDUCTED IN ATMECE

TechAvishkar 2.0, a 24-hour National Level Hackathon hosted by ATME College of Engineering, Mysuru, unfolded over two dynamic days, drawing an enthusiastic turnout of participants and distinguished guests. Presided over by Dr. Basavaraj L, Principal of ATMECE, and convened by Dr. S R Bhagyashree, Dean of Research, ATMECE, the event reflected the institution’s commitment to fostering innovation and technical excellence. The hackathon was meticulously organized under the guidance of Dr. Vinod Kumar P, IEEE Student Branch Counsellor, and Ms. Khateeja Ambareen, IEEE ATMECE Faculty Coordinator. The event began with the registration process at 8:30 AM on May 8, 2025, where 50 teams comprising approximately 197 students from various colleges across the country registered and received welcome kits. The hackathon officially commenced at 9:30 AM, setting the stage for a high-energy, innovation-driven experience.
