dean-academics.description: Dean-Academics Affairs will act in consultation with the Head of the Institute, for the all-round Academic Development of the Institute. The Roles &
dean-academics.markdown:
[Skip to content](/p/dean-academics) [![ATME College of Engineering](/__l5e/assets-v1/4519b204-1c5c-4570-ad02-6e238e674849/ATME-Final-logo-copy.png)](/p/) #### **For Job code Dean – Academics** | | | | --- | --- | | **The Job:** | **Dean – Academics** | | **Education:** | | | **Experience:** | | | **Location:** | Mysuru | | **Employment Type:** | **Permanent** | | **Roles and Responsibilities:** | Dean-Academics Affairs will act in consultation with the Head of the Institute, for the all-round Academic Development of the Institute. The Roles & Responsibility of Dean-Academic Affairs is as follows.
01. Admission and enrolment of students.
02. To Plan for the new academic programme as per the decision of the Governing Council in getting approval from concerned statutory bodies, getting affiliation from the University.
03. Finalisation of the academic calendar, time-table, registration of students for the course and examinations, classroom arrangements and all other requirements for the proper conduct of classwork.
04. Reviewing Course module & Lesson plan.
05. Reviewing Course Outcomes, Mapping of CO with PO & PSOs, PAM and the Curriculum Gap as per NBA.
06. Plan, Schedule, execute all the processes related to accreditation of various bodies.
07. Identifying the gaps in meeting any of the requirement of any of the criteria prior in hand and informing higher authorities regarding the same and also ensuring that appropriate actions are taken to fulfill the requirement.
08. Conduct of class tests and coordinating the finalization of the session’s evaluations and for ensuring the timely declaration of results.
09. Supervision of the maintenance of up-to-date academic records of all categories of students.
10. Coordinating with merit scholarship of students.
11. Organizing meetings of all the Institute level academic bodies.
12. Arranging the issue of all academic certificates, medals and prizes to the students.
13. To arrange for the conduct of those examinations which are to be conducted by the Institute as stipulated by VTU.
14. To coordinate for the conduct of Graduation Day.
15. Faculty appraisal & deputation of faculties for FDPs /Training
16. Setting up of new labs & arranging for consumable.
17. Planning co-curricular activities.
18. Periodical MIS report to Management.
19. principal.title: Principal
principal.description: The responsibilities of the Head of the Institution as an ex-officio Member Secretary in relation to Governing Council apart from mentioned earlier regarding
principal.markdown:
[Skip to content](/p/principal) [![ATME College of Engineering](/__l5e/assets-v1/4519b204-1c5c-4570-ad02-6e238e674849/ATME-Final-logo-copy.png)](/p/) #### **For Job code Principal** | | | | --- | --- | | **The Job:** | **Principal** | | **Education:** | | | **Experience:** | | | **Location:** | Mysuru | | **Employment Type:** | **Permanent** | | **Roles and Responsibilities:** | The responsibilities of the Head of the Institution as an ex-officio Member Secretary in relation to Governing Council apart from mentioned earlier regarding the conduct of Governing Council are:
01. Implementing the decisions of the Governing Council or ensuring that they are implemented through the relevant part of the institution’s management structure
02. Initiating discussion and consultation including, where appropriate, consultation with the staff and the academic council on proposals concerning the institution’s future development and ensuring that such proposals are presented to the Governing Council.
03. Apart from the responsibilities as Member Secretary of the Governing Council, the Head of the Institution serves as the educational leader, responsible for implementation of institute’s Philosophy, Vision, Mission, Values and goals adhering the provision of concerned statutory authorities. Following are some of such responsibilities.
04. Develop, manage, evaluate and supervise effective and clear procedures for the operation and functioning of the Institute consistent with the philosophy, mission, values and goals of the Institute including instructional programs, extracurricular activities, and discipline systems to ensure a safe and orderly climate, personnel management, office operations, etc.
05. Ensure compliance with all laws, policies & provisions of concerned statutory bodies and civil regulations.
06. Establish the annual master schedule / calendar of events for instructional programs as well as co-curricular activities ensuring sequential learning experiences for students.
07. Supervise the instructional programs of the Institute, evaluating lesson plans and observing classes on a regular basis to suggest corrective measure & encourage the faculty to use of a variety of instructional strategies and materials.
08. Supervise in a fair and consistent manner effective discipline and attendance systems among students & staff.
09. Establish a professional rapport with students and with staff that has their respect. Display the highest ethical and professional behavior and standards when working with students, parents and Institute personnel. Serve as a role model for students, dressing professionally, demonstrating the importance and relevance of learning, accepting responsibility, and demonstrating pride in the education profession. Encourage all teachers to do the same.
10. Keep the Board advised of employees not meeting their contractual agreement.
11. Keep the staff informed and seek ideas & suggestion for the improvement of the Institute. Conduct meetings, as necessary, for the proper functioning of the Institute: weekly meetings with Head of the Departments; monthly meeting with all the staff. Documentation proceeding of the meeting needs to be done for effective follow up.
12. Maintain visibility with students, teachers & parents. Communicate regularly with parents, seeking their support and advice, so as to create a cooperative relationship to support the student in the Institute.
13. Complete in a timely fashion all records and reports as requested by the Board. Interact with the Board regularly about the needs, successes and general operation of the Institute. All proposals to Management shall be thoroughly evaluated and a proper recommendation indicating advantages & disadvantages to the Institute.
14. To face and present the Institute before various committees visiting the Institute for the purpose of according approval, affiliation, accreditation and recognition.
15. To interact with university for exam related works and smooth conducting of examination in the Institute.
16. As ex officio member secretary of Governing Council responsible for convening the GC meeting, preparing agenda and ATR (action taken report), smooth conduction, reporting & ratification, recording minutes of the meeting and follow up for implementation of the decision taken in the meeting.

## Anti Ragging Policy

#### [RAGGING: PROHIBITION, PREVENTION AND PUNISHMENT](/p/anti-ragging-committee-2017-18)

In 2009, University Grants Commission (UGC) passed UGC REGULATION ON CURBING THE MENACE OF RAGGING IN HIGHER EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, 2009.These regulation mandate every college responsibility to curb the menace of ragging, including strict pre-emptive measures, like lodging fresher’s in a separate hostel, surprise raids especially at nights by the anti-ragging squad and submission of affidavits by all senior students and their parents taking oath not to indulge in ragging.

In view of above regulation on curbing the menace of Ragging, the under signed has formed Anti Ragging Committee (ARC) and Anti Ragging Squad Committee (ARSC) constituting a Chairman and members. ARC Chairman is being authorized to implement stringent measure and ensure discipline, ensure there are no instances of Ragging in the college campus.

If any instances of Ragging are found Chairman shall take appropriate measures immediately and submit a detailed action taken report to the Principal.

ARC Chairman has to conduct regular meeting with ARC members along with ARCS committee members. In the meeting they are instructed to review / update the status of the ground realities and submit a report to the principal annually.

#### [A BRIEF SKETCH OF WHAT CONSTITUTES RAGGING AND MEASURES TO BE TAKEN TO CURB MENACE OF RAGGING ARE FURNISHED BELOW.](/p/anti-ragging-committee-2017-18)

- Forms of Ragging: Display of noisy, disorderly conduct, teasing, excitement by rough or rude treatment or handling, including rowdy, undisciplined activities which cause or likely to cause annoyance, undue hardship, physical or psychological harm or raise apprehensive fear in a fresher, or asking the students to do any act or perform something which such a student will not do in the ordinary course and which causes him/her shame or embarrassment or danger to his/her life, etc.

- Any conduct by any student or students whether by words spoken or written or by an act which has the effect of teasing, treating or handling with rudeness a fresher or any other student.

- Indulging in rowdy or indiscipline activities by any student or students which causes or is likely to cause annoyance, hardship, physical or psychological harm or to raise fear or apprehension thereof in any fresher or any other student;

- Asking any student to do any act which such student will not in the ordinary course do and which has the effect of causing or generating a sense of shame, or torment or embarrassment so as to adversely affect the physique or psyche of such fresher or any other student.

- Any act by a senior student that prevents, disrupts or disturbs the regular academic activity of any other student or a fresher;

- Any act of financial extortion or forceful expenditure burden put on a fresher or any other student by students;

- Any act of physical abuse including all variants of it: sexual abuse, homosexual assaults, stripping, forcing obscene and lewd acts, gestures, causing bodily harm or any other danger to health or person;

- Any act or abuse by spoken words, emails, post, public insults which would also include deriving perverted pleasure, vicarious or sadistic thrill from actively or passively participating in the discomfiture to fresher or any other student;

- Any act that affects the mental health and self-confidence of a fresher or any other student. With or without an intent to derive a sadistic pleasure or showing off power, authority or superiority by a student over any fresher or any other student.

#### [ACTION TO BE TAKEN BY THE HEAD OF THE INSTITUTION](/p/anti-ragging-committee-2017-18)

On receipt of the recommendation of the Anti-Ragging Squad or on receipt of any information concerning any reported incident of ragging, the Head of Institution shall immediately determine if a case under the penal laws is made and if so, either on his own or through a member of the Anti-Ragging Committee authorized by him in this behalf, proceed to file a First Information Report (FIR), within twenty four hours of receipt of such information or recommendation, with the police and local authorities, under the appropriate penal provisions relating to one or more of the following, namely;

i. Abetment to ragging

ii. Criminal conspiracy to rag

iii. Unlawful assembly and rioting while ragging

iv. Public nuisance created during ragging

v. Violation of decency and morals through ragging

vi. Injury to body, causing hurt or grievous hurt

vii. Wrongful restraint

viii. Wrongful confinement

ix. Use of criminal force

x. Assault as well as sexual offences or unnatural offences

xi. Extortion

xii. Criminal trespass

xiii. Offences against property

xiv. Criminal intimidation

xv. Attempts to commit any or all of the above mentioned offences against the victim(s)

xvi. Threat to commit any or all of the above mentioned offences against the victim(s)

xvii. Physical or psychological humiliation

#### [ADMINISTRATIVE ACTION IN THE EVENT OF RAGGING](/p/anti-ragging-committee-2017-18)

The institution shall punish a student found guilty of ragging after following the procedure and in the manner prescribed herein under: –

a. The Anti-Ragging Committee of the institution shall take an appropriate decision, in regard to punishment or otherwise, depending on the facts of each incident of ragging and nature and gravity of the incident of ragging established in the recommendations of the Anti-Ragging Squad.

b. The Anti-Ragging Committee may, depending on the nature and gravity of the guilt established by the Anti-Ragging Squad, award, to those found guilty, one or more of the following punishments, namely;

i. Suspension from attending classes and academic privileges.

ii. Withholding/withdrawing scholarship/fellowship and other benefits.

iii. Debarring from appearing in any test/examination or other evaluation process.

iv. Withholding results.

v. Debarring from representing the institution in any regional, national or international meet, tournament, youth festival etc.

vi. Suspension/expulsion from the hostel.

vii. Cancellation of admission

viii. Rustication from the institution for period ranging from one to four semesters.

ix. Expulsion from the institution and consequent debarring from admission to any other institution for a specified period.

x. Fine up to 25000/-

#### [IN THE EVENT OF PERSONS COMMITTING OR ABETTING THE ACT OF RAGGING IS NOT IDENTIFIED, THE INSTITUTION SHALL RESORT TO COLLECTIVE PUNISHMENT.](/p/anti-ragging-committee-2017-18)

c. An appeal against the order of punishment by the Anti-Ragging Committee shall lie,

1. In case of an order of an institution, affiliated to or constituent part, of a University, to the Vice Chancellor of the University.
2. In case of an order of University, to its Chancellor
3. In case of an institution of national importance created by an Act of Parliament, to the Chairman or Chancellor of the institution, as the case may be.

#### [RESPONSIBILITIES OF SQUADS IN CHARGE OF ANTI-RAGGING COMMITTEE](/p/anti-ragging-committee-2017-18)

Squads In charge will be Responsible for the following in their areas:

1. Ensure display of anti-ragging instructions sign boards at the prominent places in the College campus

2. They will form duty chart & carryout regular checks for any Ragging activity in the campus.

3. Squad In charge will maintain the proper duty attendance register in respect of the members of the squad and their duties.

4. They will carry out surprise checks in probable areas of ragging.

5. In case of any incidence noticed they have to inform their chairman for further action.

6. Squad in charge will brief all members of his squad about their duties / action regarding anti ragging.

7. All squad members should forward a feedback report to their chairman daily before 11.00 AM & 4.00PM.

8. The squad in charge will collect the updated list of student including their latest address and phone no’s in respect of the classes run in their blocks of their areas.

9. The chairman has to conduct regular meeting with their members, submit the report to the Principal annually.

#### [ANTI RAGGING COMMITTEE](/p/anti-ragging-committee-2017-18)

testimonial-3.title: Testimonial 3
testimonial-3.markdown:
[Skip to content](/p/testimonial-3)

[![ATME College of Engineering](/__l5e/assets-v1/4519b204-1c5c-4570-ad02-6e238e674849/ATME-Final-logo-copy.png)](/p/)

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2017/10/VEDASWI-PV-1-92x92.jpg)

### VEDASWI PV

2nd Year, ECE

The relationship between faculty & students is cordial. Here faculties make the college what it is today with a positive attitude, being knowledgeable , approachable & readily available to the students in their needs.

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2017/10/Sara-Simran-1-92x92.jpg)

### Sara Simran

3rd Year, ECE

Quality of teaching is good, the faculty are reputed and understanding. The curriculum is in par with the latest trends in education and the faculties are constantly improving with the ever-evolving educational practices. One can always get their problems solved without any hesitation. They are the Spark that makes me study and ready for job placements.

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2017/10/Chingakham-Romita-Chanu-1-92x92.jpg)

### Chingakham Romita Chanu

4th Year, ECE

The teachers are great, enthusiastic and caring. The teachers make sure the students understand the topics by taking the example of real-world applications so the classes are interactive. They are concerned about students' careers and always take time and go out of the way  even under busy schedules for students who need them.

## Celebration of National Pollution Control Day

National Pollution Control Day 2021 is observed annually on December 2.  It is a day to raise awareness about the hazards of air pollution. On the Account of National Pollution Control Day, the NSS wing of ATME College of Engineering organised the plantation of saplings in the college premises.

Dr. L Basavaraj, Principal, ATMECE, Dr. M.S Govinde Gowda, Dean Academics, Dr. Bhagyashree S R, Dean Research, and Dr. Sachidanandamurthy K L Administrative Officer were present during the event. The Principal addressed the gathering conveying the importance of Environmental Pollution Control and advised all to have a continuous approach towards this goal.

[**REPORT**](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/report-on-POLLUTION-CONTROL-DAY.pdf)

human-rights-day.description: CICC-College Internal Complaints Committee, ATME College of engineering. Mysuru  has been organized “World Human Rights Day” on 10th Dec-2021 in its campus.
human-rights-day.markdown:
[Skip to content](/p/human-rights-day)

[![ATME College of Engineering](/__l5e/assets-v1/4519b204-1c5c-4570-ad02-6e238e674849/ATME-Final-logo-copy.png)](/p/)

![](/__l5e/assets-v1/f3fc5e4a-71e8-48df-ae67-dc95d89c569e/4.jpg)

## HUMAN RIGHTS DAY

CICC-College Internal Complaints Committee, ATME College of engineering. Mysuru  has been organized “World Human Rights Day” on 10th Dec-2021 in its campus.

On this occasion more than 800 Students from various departments along with the Staff members of ATMECE took the pledge on “Human Rights”  to uphold the values of  Human Rights  and to be a constructive citizen for the development of the country.

The pledge was administered by Dr. Bhagyashree S R Chairperson CICC, and the program was coordinated by Mr. Chandrashekar C, Member Secretary CICC, under the guidance of  Principal Dr.L.Basavaraj,

During the occasion Dr.M.S.Govindegowda-Dean student Affairs,  spoke about the meaning of Human Rights and importance of Human Rights Day celebration.

Dr.Basavaraj.L Principal, Dr.G.Rathnakar-Dean Student affairs, Dr.Sachidananda Administrative Officer, Heads of various departments, Staff members and Students were present during the program.

new-exam-schedules-for-diploma.description: Engineering colleges train graduates in their respective branch/ department of study, have a holistic outlook towards life, and have a desire to work for
new-exam-schedules-for-diploma.markdown:
[Skip to content](/p/new-exam-schedules-for-diploma)

[![ATME College of Engineering](/__l5e/assets-v1/4519b204-1c5c-4570-ad02-6e238e674849/ATME-Final-logo-copy.png)](/p/)

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/2.jpeg)

Engineering colleges train graduates in their respective branch/ department of study, have a holistic outlook towards life, and have a desire to work for national needs and beyond. The graduating student must have excellent knowledge and skills in the area of his study. However, he must also have broad understanding of society and relationships.

Character needs to be nurtured as an essential quality by which he would understand and fulfil his responsibility as an engineer, a citizen and a human being.

Besides the above, several meta-skills and underlying values are needed. In this endeavour to build the morale among the students as directed by AICTE and MOE induction program was conducted for the newly admitted 1st year students for the academic year 2021-2022 batch.

**Report :** [Link](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/REPORT-SIP-2021-1.pdf)

new-exam-schedules-for-diploma-2.description: NSS Unit of ATME College of Engineering, Bannuru Road, Mysuru, was organized a Webinar on “Patriotism & Moral Education” by Swami Shivakantanada Ji,

[![ATME College of Engineering](/__l5e/assets-v1/4519b204-1c5c-4570-ad02-6e238e674849/ATME-Final-logo-copy.png)](/p/)

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/1.jpeg)

NSS Unit of ATME College of Engineering, Bannuru Road, Mysuru, was organized a Webinar on “Patriotism & Moral Education” by Swami Shivakantanada Ji, Correspondent, RIMSE, Mysuru in commemoration of “Republic Day“and 75th Independence Day “Azadi Ka Amruth Mahothsav”.

Resource person His holiness Swami Shivakantananda Ji in his discourse he shared his thoughts “Patriotism is the feeling of attachment and love to one’s country. It encompasses devotion and robust support for the nation. Love and dedication towards a country is an integral part of our growth of the nation. Moral values are very important in shaping integrity and virtues in the society.

When integrated in the Education system, more-so from the early stages, it can really go along in building a patriotic and virtuous society. Moral, ethical and social values are very essential to be taught for children at an early time of their development so that they become deeply rooted in their lives” More than 250 students along with Staff members were participated in the webinar, Dr Rathnakar G, Dean Student Affairs, ATMECE, and Mr. Chandrashekar C, Faculty Dept of Humanities, Mr. Rudresh A.N, Faculty Dept of Civil & NSS Program Officer and Mrs. Shruthi H G Faculty Dept of Civil Coordinated the entire event.

new-exam-schedules-for-diploma-2-2.title: Atal Ranking of Institutions on Innovation Achievements (ARIIA)
new-exam-schedules-for-diploma-2-2.description: Atal Ranking of Institutions on Innovation Achievements (ARIIA) is a path-breaking policy initiative of the Ministry of Education (MoE), Govt. of India
new-exam-schedules-for-diploma-2-2.markdown:
[Skip to content](/p/new-exam-schedules-for-diploma-2-2)

[![ATME College of Engineering](/__l5e/assets-v1/4519b204-1c5c-4570-ad02-6e238e674849/ATME-Final-logo-copy.png)](/p/)

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/rsz_2industrial_automation_banner-03.jpg)

Atal Ranking of Institutions on Innovation Achievements (ARIIA) is a path-breaking policy initiative of the Ministry of Education (MoE), Govt. of India implemented through AICTE and MoE’s Innovation Cell to systematically rank all major higher educational institutions and universities in India on indicators related to promotion and support of “Innovation and Entrepreneurship Development” amongst students and faculties.

Below are the major parameters considered in ARIIA for ranking:

- Activities to promote and support innovation & start-up in the campus
- Pre-incubation and incubation infrastructures & facilities available in campus
- Academic courses offered by the institute on innovation, IPR and start-up
- Successful innovation and start-ups emerged from campus
- Investment, collaboration and partnerships with ecosystem enablers
- Research outputs; publications and intellectual properties generated
- Technology transfer and commercialization efforts

The very first edition of ARIIA started in 2019 and total 496 institutes competed to get a position in the ranking. The result was announced on 8th April 2019 in presence of Hon’ble President of India has announced the names. For the 2nd edition of ARIIA (2020), a total of 674 institutes were participated and rankings were announced by Hon’ble Vice-President of India on 18th August 2020. The current edition of ARIIA 2021 saw unprecedented participation as compared to earlier two editions. Out of total of 3551 HEIs registered, 1438 institutions (including all IITs, NITs, IISc, etc.) participated which is more than double as compared to 2nd edition and approximately 4 times as compared to the first edition. This 3rd edition of ARIIA has introduced a special framework for non-technical institutions that further strengthen the innovation and entrepreneurial ecosystem in Indian higher education institutions.

ARIIA 2021 classify participating institutions into under two major categories; Technical and Non-technical. The technical category has following 5 sub-categories;

1. CFTIs, Central University, & Institute of National Importance
2. State University & Deemed University (Govt. & Govt. Aided)
3. Govt. College/Institution (Govt. & Govt. Aided)
4. University & Deemed University (Self-Finance/Private)
5. Private College/Institute (Self-Finance/Private)

All these submitted applications were subjected to multiple stages of screening, validation evaluation as per the ARIIA framework and guideline developed by the evaluation committee. Based on the score and range developed for the parameters and sub-parameters and category wise score and rank prepared for HEIs. Top-performing technical and non-technical HEIs assigned with a rank and band of ‘Outstanding’ whereas all the remaining technical and non-technical institutions in each category assigned a band of either ‘Excellent’ ‘Performer’, ‘Promising’ or ‘Beginner’ to encourage their effort and participation in ARIIA.

We are proud to announce that Academy for Technical and Management Excellence (ATME) college of Engineering is listed under Band-Beginner.

a-report-on-international-yoga-day.markdown:

[![ATME College of Engineering](/__l5e/assets-v1/4519b204-1c5c-4570-ad02-6e238e674849/ATME-Final-logo-copy.png)](/p/)

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/yoga_day_banner-01.jpg)

NSS unit of ATME College of Engineering organised a International Yoga Day on 21st June 2022. The Yoga session started with the opening address of Dr. M S Govinde Gowda, Dean (Academics), welcomed the participants and emphasized the need and importance of yoga in the daily life.

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/yd1-300x201.jpg)

Dr. Suresh Kumar S, Associate Professor, Dept of Mechanical Engineering, ATMECE, has carried the Yoga practice session. The Yoga session started with a basic introduction of Yoga, Pranayama and Dhyana and their implementation in day-to-day lives, practical demonstration of Sukshama Vyayama, Surya Namaskar, Kapalbhati and Bhastrika Pranayama and various Asanas. All Students and Faculties from different streams are participated in the session. They enjoyed the session fully and were greatly benefitted. As a feedback, the participants appreciated the event.

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/yd2-300x225.jpg)

The event was coordinated by Mr. Rudresh A N, NSS Program Officer, Mr. Devaraj M R, Associate Professor, Mr. Yathisha N, Assistant Professor and Dr. Muralidhar M P, PDE under the guidance and support of Dr. M S Govinde Gowda, Dean Academics and Dr. Sachidanandamurthy K L, Administrative Officer, ATMECE.

The programme was ended with thanking all the participants.

state-level-technical-fest-avagamah-2022.markdown:
[Skip to content](/p/state-level-technical-fest-avagamah-2022)

[![ATME College of Engineering](/__l5e/assets-v1/4519b204-1c5c-4570-ad02-6e238e674849/ATME-Final-logo-copy.png)](/p/)

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/State-Level-Technical-Fest-banner-02.jpg)

**About the College**

ATME college of engineering is founded by a group of like-minded technocrats in 2010. Founders are managing various kind of enterprises like infra companies, manufacturing units, and IT service. Founders are aware of the need of the industry and trying to cater to such needs by developing industry-ready engineers through ATME College of Engineers.

ATME has been fostering Industry-Institute interaction on a regular basis. ATMECE has entered to MOUs with many industries for Internships, Placement, Skill enhancement, Research & Development etc., Reputed companies like CISCO, Texas Instruments, Frenus Technologies have set up their labs and Training centers in the college campus

ATME College of Engineering is rated ‘GOLD’ by QS I·GAUGE for its Overall Excellence as a top-notch College and has become the 1st College in Mysuru to be awarded in Engineering Category.

ATME has created an ecosystem where education is just not limited to academics, it extends beyond the class rooms & labs to industry interactions, cultural, social and sports events for the all-round development of the students.

**About the Department**

The Department of Electrical & Electronics Engineering was started in the year 2010 with an intake of 60 students. The department with its strong pool of faculty, well-developed laboratories and latest software and hardware facilities emphasizes towards imparting quality education, hands-on expertise to students to shape their all-round personality. The Department offers UG program in Electrical & Electronics Engineering which is accredited by NBA under MHRD. The department is also recognized as research centre by VTU.

Quantum is a technical forum for students to exhibit their technical abilities through their project works,

seminars and quiz activities.

**Event 1: State Level Technical Project Exhibition**

**Exhibition Date:** 29.6.2022

**Venue :** Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering.

**Objective:**

- To provide platform to showcase student’s technical ability.
- To propel the creativity from the students.
- To create awareness about the latest researches, challenges of the society & inventions in the stream of Electrical & Electronics
- To test the applications of the concepts that has been learned

**Eligibility, Rules and** **Guidelines:**

- Final year students from Engineering and Diploma institutions.
- Branches: Electrical & Electronics Engineering, Electronics & Communication Engineering, Instrumentation Technology, Telecommunication Engineering, Electronics & Instrumentation Technology.
- The Project team shall have a maximum of 4 students
- Projects will be evaluated by experts Committee.
- Participants must Exhibit their Modules
- Participants should bring all required materials to exhibit their hardware / software projects. The Electric power supply will be made available.
- Commercially procured kits or models should not constitute a major portion of the project.
- Student must set up their project, remain with it throughout their judging period and remove it at the end of the exhibition
- All Participants have to submit one copy of Project report(spiral bound) containing Project Title, Introduction, objective’s, Block diagram, brief description, Advantages and disadvantages, , Applications, Results, conclusion and future scope duly signed by their guide, HoD.
- Registration will open till 27th June 2022.
- E-Certificate to all participants.
- No TA/DA is admissible. Accommodation will be provided on their own cost with prior intimation
- Top 3 Best Projects will be awarded with: Cash prize and Winners Certificate
- Registration Fee: Rs.300 per Project team.
- Registration Fee Payment as to be done to Account No. 12103100008499, Account Name: ATME EEE DEPARTMENT’, Karnataka Gramin bank, Mellahally, Mysuru.
- Registration Link:  [https://forms.gle/B5diWQSSuJn9gqRu8](https://forms.gle/B5diWQSSuJn9gqRu8)
- Scan QR Code for registration of Event 1: State Level Technical Project Exhibition![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/qr-2-150x150.png)

ATME College of Engineering, Mysuru has organized a webinar on the topic “Why Intellectual Property is important for Academia?” in association with Institutions Innovation Council on 30th July 2021. Dr. Nithin K S, shared about the concepts of Intellectual Property, its types and importance in academia in detail through the Webinar.

## ATMECE CONDUCTED 5 DAYS NSS CAMP AT BILIGERE HUNDI VILLAGE

The NSS wing of the ATME College of Engineering, Bannur Road, Mysuru, conducted a Camp for five days at the Biligere Hundi Village, T.Narasipura Taluk, Mysuru. More than 30 students participated actively in the NSS Camp and extended a good service for the health, hygiene and welfare of the village.

The camp was inaugurated by Sri. Basavarajappa, a senior resident of the Biligere Hundi village by lightening the lamp and appreciated the venture. The NSS volunteers carried out various social activities like Plantation of saplings, Arrangement and management of a Blood donation camp along with blood donation by themselves, a Health Check-up Camp for diabetes and Blood Pressure, Cleaning of Roads surroundings of the village and cleaning of the temple and so on as day activities while during evenings, awareness speeches were arranged by eminent personalities on topics such as self-cleanliness of school students, importance of continued education after SSLC, use of Bio-fuels, Rainwater Harvesting, Bank loans, Subsidies and Insurance policies that are available for farmers, precautions to be observed for facing the 3rd wave of Covid-19.

The NSS Camp was organised by Mr. Rudresh A N, The Program Officer, along with the other faculty coordinators, Mrs. Harshitha N, Dr. Muralidhar M P, Dr. Sathish K R, Mr. Raghu, Mr. Dhananjaya and Mr. Raghavendra, with the guidance and support of Dr. L Basavaraj, Principal, ATMECE, Dr. M.S. Govindegowda Dean Academics,Dr. Rathnakar G, Dean-Student Affairs and Administrative officer Dr.Sachidananda. On the last day of the camp, a valedictory function was arranged in which Mr. Mariswamy, BEO, Mr. Ramesh, PDO, Dr. Rathnakar G, Dean-Student Affairs, ATMECE.

[**Detailed Report**](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/Detailed-Report-1-16.pdf)

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/31.jpg)

## ATMEs’ MoU with IIT-Guwahati

ATME as on the 16th of December 2020 signed an MoU with Electronics and ICT Academy (IIT-Guwahati). The MoU is towards making ATME an Academic Partner for their mutual interest in the fields of training, education, research and development, and as a contribution to increased national cooperation.

As a part of the MoU, the two organizations shall work together for:

- Collaboration in teaching and training for various courses.
- Academic specific training programmes or courses
- Development of the new courses and training modules for enhancing the employability for stakeholders.
- Collaboration in research and development, and consultancy works.
- Exchange of academic & research materials and joint publications.
- Cooperation in projects, research activities of mutual interest.
- Publication of Intellectual properties (IPs) developed jointly through project/research collaboration.
- Participation in seminars, colloquia, and other types of academic discussions

The MoU process was signed by Dr. L. Basavaraj, Principal, ATMECE, Mysuru, Prof. Ratnajit Bhattacharjee, Principal Investigator, E&ICT Academy, IIT Guwahati and Prof. Gopal Das, Dean -R&D, IIT Guwahati.

## Graduation Day-2021

ATME College of Engineering Celebrated the Graduation Day on 25th Aug 2021. The main  purpose of a Graduation ceremony is to celebrate students who have successfully met the  academic and extracurricular requirements for graduation. The ceremony provides a  public venue in which graduating students receive their Course completion certificate,  marking their official graduation from the institution.

In the celebration about 600 students from the AY 2019-20 & AY 2020-21 passed out  batches were present in the event.

**Brief of the Event:**

The ceremony begins with the entry of the procession with Honourable Guests Dr. J  Shashidhar Prasad, Former Vice-Chancellor, University of Mysore and Mr. Raghavendra  Kadkol, Senior Principal, Employee Relations, Infosys along with the Governing Council  members of the Institution enters the auditorium and respects the National anthem and  Nadageethe.

Principal Sir welcomed the dignitaries, Guests and governing council members and gave  a brief report about the institution. Then Honourable Chairman opened the graduation  day, after that department wise students were called to receive the course completion  certificate. Institute celebrated the Graduation day by following the SOP issued by  Government of Karnataka.

Whole event was streamed on YouTube for the public and Many parents were facilitated  to watch the event celebration in live streaming at several ICT enabled classrooms in the  campus.

Class wise group photos were captured where the all the staffs of the departments, Deans,  Principal and management members were present.

## Computer Science & Design

**About the Department**

**Intake of the Department = 60**

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Dr.-Nasreen-Fathima-2.jpg)Computing and computer technology have become integral to nearly every aspect of our daily lives, with a rising demand for digital tools and applications across various sectors. The fusion of creativity, design, and software development skills is now more sought after than ever. Beyond mere coding, Computer Science and Design (CSD) represent a burgeoning research area, utilizing computational tools to extract, filter, and create knowledge to support professional endeavors.

The significance of Interaction Design and Design Methods is rapidly growing in IT products and services, aligning with the heightened focus on user experience. This program covers a diverse range of subjects, including Programming Languages, Software Development, Website Construction, Image Processing, Spatial Computing, Media Computing, Animation and Graphics, Game Design and Development, and Fundamentals of Video and Photography for Engineers.

Our Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science and Design is designed to prepare students for thriving careers in the IT industry, digital design, and media sectors such as gaming, animation, virtual/augmented reality, user interfaces, robotics, entertainment, and digital analytics. The curriculum not only equips students for immediate industry roles but also lays a solid foundation for further studies in Computer Science or Design.

This course emphasizes the development of techniques and abilities to address problems through a Human-Computer Interaction design process. I extend a warm invitation to all prospective students to join this innovative branch, where together, we can form a creative team that makes a positive difference.

### NABL ACCREDITED

### ATME CIVIL ENGINEERING MATERIAL TESTING FACILITY (MECHANICAL)

* * *

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/nabl-banner-03.jpg)

The ATME Civil Engineering Material Testing Laboratory is dedicated to ensuring top quality testing services for Civil Engineering materials. The Civil Engineering Department offers a wide range of services, including:

- **Soil Testing**

- **Sub-Soil Investigation**

- **Highway Materials Testing**

- **Concrete & Reinforced Structure Testing**

- **Non-Destructive Testing**

- **Third-Party Inspections for Quality Control and Assurance**

- **Consultancy Services etc**

The department is established in a 800 sq. ft. laboratory, fully equipped with the latest testing equipment for accurate soil and material analysis. To ensure top-notch service, all testing equipment and machinery are regularly calibrated and maintained by an NABL-approved laboratory, overseen by engineers with extensive experience in quality control across various fields.

Civil department is having competent workforce having with qualifications ranging from Doctorates, Post Graduate, Graduate and Diploma levels. Continuous training is provided to employees to further enhance their expertise. All tests are conducted in compliance with relevant National and International Standards. Clients recognize the Civil Department for its high-quality work, excellent services, and effective problem-solving solutions.

* * *

### Our proud clients

- Skill Tech Engineers and contractors Pvt. ltd Mysore.
- Vision structural design Aid (Bangalore)
- Mytech estate developer’s builder’s Pvt. limited Mysore.
- Bunts Sangha Mysore charitable trust (Regd).
- Citizen welfare society, Mysore.
- Ramakrishna house building co- operative society

* * *

#### Contact Details

Head of the Department,

Department of Civil Engineering

ATME College of Engineering, Mysore

**Phone No: [+91-9738806913](tel:+919738806913)**

[Quality Policy](/p/nabl)

#### Quality Policy

The Quality Policy of ATMECE Material Testing Lab is committed to providing services that fully satisfy customer expectations. The organization is focused on meeting customer needs and continuously improving the effectiveness of its Quality Management System (QMS). Management routinely reviews operations to ensure that working methods , available instruments , and the skills of technicians are adequate to deliver accurate and timely results.

#### Objectives

- Ensure all testing instruments are calibrated and valid for each sample tested
- Complete sample testing within 15 working days
- Use analytical standards traceable to certified reference materials.

[Designs & Proof Checking](/p/nabl)

#### Designs & Proof Checking

**Conducting proof checking and peer reviews of structural designs and drawings for buildings and other structure:**

- Ensure the accuracy and quality of design outputs.
- Reviewing soil investigation data for accuracy and relevance.
- Assess load-bearing elements and stress management.
- Verifying compliance with relevant codes and standards related to loadings and design procedures.
- Performing independent 3D analysis to assess the structure’s behaviour.
- Evaluating the safety of the structure, as well as the cost-effectiveness of member sizes and reinforcement.
- Utilized software tools include STAADPRO, AUTOCAD, and in-house Excel sheets.

[![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/1nabl.jpg)](/p/nabl/1nabl)

[Geotechnical Investigations Scope](/p/nabl)

#### Geotechnical Investigations Scope

- Field investigations and site assessments
- Laboratory testing of materials
- Analysis and recommendations for foundation systems
- Design of ground improvement techniques
- Design of earth structures
- Quality control for earthworks

#### Laboratory Testing

- Moisture Content
- Water Absorption
- Specific Gravity (Pycnometer & Density Bottle)
- Free Swell Ratio
- Grain Size Analysis
  - Sieve Analysis (Dry & Wet)
- Field Density Test
  - Core Cutter
  - Sand Replacement Method
- Compaction Test (MDD & OMC)
  - Light Compaction
  - Heavy Compaction
- Atterberg’s Limits
  - Liquid Limit
  - Plastic Limit
  - Shrinkage Limit
- Direct Shear Test (Cohesion & Angle of Internal Friction)
- Unconfined Compressive Strength Test
- Laboratory Permeability Test
  - Fine Grained Soil
  - Coarse Grained Soil
- Laboratory C.B.R. Test
  - Light Compaction (Soaked & Unsoaked)
  - Heavy Compaction (Soaked & Unsoaked)

Conducting tests on a wide range of building materials, including bitumen, cement, concrete mix designs, and geotechnical materials.

- Equipped with advanced, state-of-the-art testing equipment.
- Expertise and facilities to perform testing of construction materials in compliance with BIS, ASTM, BS, EN, MORTH, NHAI, Railway, CPWD, DRDO, and FIP specifications

Structural Steel

- Cement – Physical
- Flyash

- Concrete Paver Block Water Absorption

#### Concrete Mix Proportioning

- Standard Concrete – M20 to M55
- High Strength/ High Performance Concrete- M60 to M80
- Self-Compacting Concrete

#### Testing of Flooring Materials

- **Ceramic/Vitrified Tiles**
- **Brick Testing**

Physical Test:

- Colour
- Soundness
- Hardness
- Size & Shape)
- Crushing Strength Test
- Water Absorption Test

#### FINE AND COARSE AGGREGATE TESTING

- Gradation Test
- Specific Gravity
- Material Finer Than 75 Micron
- Water Absorption
- Bulk Density & Voids
- Crushing Strength
- Los Angeles Abrasion Test
- Impact Strength
- Determination of Aggregate Indices
- Angularity Number
- % Silt and Clay Content

#### BITUMEN TESTING

- Penetration Test
- Softening Point
- Viscosity Test
- Ductility Test

- **Assessment of quality / strength of RC members through appropriate field tests.**

#### Test Facilities

- **Rebound Hammer test (Concrete / Bricks / Mortar).**
- **Ultrasonic Pulse Velocity test.**

Monitoring construction quality through regular site visits.

Supervising quality through daily inspections and certification of bills.

#### Key Aspects:

- Construction Materials
- Construction Methodology

- Adopted Quality Standards
- Performance Test Witnessing
- Technical Support for Site Issues
- Documentation of Quality Standard

## Steps to Register for CYBERARMOR

#### [STEP - 1: INTRODUCTION](/p/cyberarmor-registration)

## About Cybersecurity Fundamentals

Cybersecurity fundamentals are the basic principles and practices used to protect computer systems, networks and data from cyber threats, unauthorized access, and attacks. It focuses on ensuring confidentiality, integrity, and availability (CIA) of information.

The Cybersecurity Fundamentals course has been designed as a structured 12-week learning program delivered through a Learning Management System (LMS) with Virtual Lab. The objective of this course is to introduce students to the essential concepts of cybersecurity and provide practical exposure to security challenges and solutions in modern digital infrastructure.

The course structure combines content-based learning, activity-based learning, self-learning modules, and virtual laboratory exercises to create a comprehensive and engaging educational experience.

## Project Background

This LMS-based course module has been developed as part of the Cybersecurity in Power Systems project funded by AICTE under the MODROB scheme. The initiative aims to modernize laboratory facilities and integrate advanced cybersecurity training tools and virtual learning environments for engineering students.

The project has been implemented at ATME College of Engineering, Mysuru, with the goal of enhancing student competencies in cybersecurity awareness, practical skills, and research in secure power system infrastructure.

## Course Structure

These modules introduce fundamental cybersecurity concepts through structured learning materials and guided activities. Each module includes learning materials, interactive activities, Practical exercises using virtual labs, short assessments to reinforce conceptual understanding.

**Students are exposed to key topics covered in Modules such as:**

**Module-1: Introduction to Cybersecurity**

**Module-2: Cyber offence**

**Module-3: Tools and Methods used in Cybersecurity**

**Module-4: Cybersecurity Resources**

**Module-5: Detecting and Evaluating IP address Vulnerabilities**

**Module-6: Simulating a Password Attack**

**Module-7: Phishing Attack Simulation**

**Module-8: Encryption and Decryption**

**Module-9: WIFI- Hacking with Evil Twin Attack**

**Module-10: Cybersecurity in Power Systems (Demo)**

**Module-11:  Networks Sniffing and Man in the Middle Attack**

**Module-12: Penetration Testing with nmap**

**Module-13: Simulating Denial of Service(DoS) Attack**

**Module-14: Building a Virtual Private Network**

## Target Audience:

- UG students
- PG students
- Graduates
- Working professionals who are interested in learning cybersecurity are eligible to enroll in this course.

## Continuous Internal Evaluation and Semester End Exam

- Each module will include a Pre-Assessment (non-graded) and a Post-Assessment, which will consist of an Assessment Quiz. The minimum passing grade is 50%.
- Each student will be given three attempts to successfully complete Post assessment under each Module.
- A final examination will be conducted at the end of the course. The schedule and details of the examination will be communicated to users through their registered email and official announcements.

## Academic Council

**Academic council ensures quality in academic activities.**

**Objective**: The Council’s main objective is to ensure a healthy academic atmosphere and enhance the learning experience for the students. It monitors the students’ academic experience and reviews.

**Structure & Constitution of the Academic Council shall be as under:**

|     |     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **ACADEMIC COUNCIL MEMBERS** |
| **Sl. No.** | **Name** | **Position** | **Contact No** |
| 1 | Dr. L BASAVARAJ | Chairman | 9448285641 |
| 2 | Dr. CHETHAN S (Associate to Dean Academics) | Member Secretary | 9844928905 |
| 3 | Dr. BHAGYASHREE S R | Member | 9900110944 |
| 4 | Dr. SRINIVASA K | Member | 9738601201 |
| 5 | Dr. PUTTE GOWDA D | Member | 9900622401 |

| 14 | Dr. SHAKUNTALA C | Member | 8970779374 |
| 15 | Dr. OSCAR ABHISHEK | Member | 9972044943 |
| 16 | Mr. SUDHAKAR N | Member | 9480573571 |
| 17 | Mrs. PRIYANKA N B | Member | 9663674218 |
| 18 | Dr. T KASAR, Founder & Director, EDspire Research. | Industry Member | 8123530082 |
| 19 | Dr. MANGALA KESHAVA, BMSCE, BANGALORE | Member | 9845675201 |

**Meetings**: The Member Secretary shall, with the approval of the Head of the Institute convene the meetings of the Academic Council at least twice in a year and on such other occasions as may be necessary. Member Secretary shall with the approval of the Head of the Institute prepare the agenda for the meeting. One half of the members shall constitute the quorum, However, if there is no quorum for the meeting up to half an hour, then the meeting shall stand adjourned to the next convenient day fixed, In the adjourned meeting, if there is no quorum for up to half an hour, then the members present shall themselves constitute the quorum and conduct the meeting.

**Roles & Responsibilities**: Without prejudice to the generality of functions mentioned, the Roles & Responsibilities of Academic Council is as under.

- Discuss and deliberate upon the affiliated University prescribed courses of study, academic regulations, curricula, scheme syllabi and modifications thereof, instructional and evaluation arrangements, methods, procedures relevant thereto and send opinion, comments and modification request to the affiliating University for its consideration.
- Adopt the Regulations regarding the admission of students consistent with the university/ Government norms to different programmes of study in the College.
- Frame Regulations consistent with the University norms for the conduct of CEA and initiate measures for improving the quality of teaching, student’s evaluation and student advisory system in the College.
- To formulate policies to improve the TLP in the Institute by promoting Innovative teaching methods, adoption of ICT tools for teaching, identifying teaching needs and arranging for the same.
- Make regulations for sports, extra-curricular activities and proper maintenance and functioning of playgrounds and hostels.
- Recommend to the Governing Body the proposals for the institution of new programmes of study at the College.
- Recommend to the Governing Body institution of scholarships, studentships, fellowships, prizes and medals and to frame regulations for award of the same.
- Advise the Governing Body on suggestions pertaining to academic affairs.
- Encourage the faculty members to undertake Sponsored Research, Industrial Consultancy, Continuing education, and related activities and
- Perform such other functions as may be assigned to it by the Governing Body.

## About ATME College of Engineering

ATME College of Engineering Mysuru, established in 2010, is recognized by AICTE New Delhi and affiliated to Visvesvaraya Technological University, Belagavi, Karnataka. The college offers 11 undergraduate programs and two postgraduate programs. ATMECE has been accredited by the National Board of Accreditation (NBA). ATMECE is NABL accredited under ISO/IEC 17025:2017 for Civil Engineering Laboratory.

The college has been honored as “The Best Emerging Private Engineering College in Karnataka” along with “Most Promising Upcoming Private Engineering Colleges in Karnataka” for two consecutive years. It also holds QS I-Gauge Gold Ranking status and has been recognized as one of the “Swachh Institutes of the Country.” ATMECE is NAAC accredited with an A+ grade and is one among seven engineering colleges in Karnataka to achieve this rating during its first cycle. All departments at the institute have established recognized research centres. The institute has secured over Rs. 5 crores in external funding for various research and consultancy projects. The institute has collaborations with more than twenty-five industries worldwide.

## About The Library

Library is like a Knowledge center and is the heart of the institute. The user’s satisfaction is the main motto of library services and it is a key success of the library.  The main role of an engineering college library is to satisfy the needs of its users.  ATMECE Library and Information center established in October 2010.  The Library attracts students, teachers, researchers, educational administrators and other users from different branches of the college.

The Library is centrally located and the state-of-the-art library is spread over 700 Sq. Mtrs in two levels with 250 seating capacity. The ground floor acts as a lending section and the first floor acts as a reference section. The reference section with a capacity of about 200 students is set against a vast expanse of greenery and is ideal for students who want to refer to books in a serene atmosphere.  The primary objective of the library is to support the educational and research programs of the institute by providing physical and online access to information, consistent with the present and the anticipated educational and research functions of the institute.

The Library is well –protected with fire alarm, CCTV-Surveillance.  It has specialized collections of Books, Journals and resources in Sciences, Engineering and Humanities, ranging from printed books, E-Books, E-Journals, Back volumes and CDs/DVDs. The Library has NPTEL and Edusat Videos.  It is a fully automated library predominantly related to Engineering, Technology and allied subjects.

**Vision**

To be an excellent storehouse for easy access to information resources for Technical learning and research through professional integrity and social responsibility.

**Mission**

To support the academic and research needs of the students and staff on par with national and international benchmarks.

**Objectives**

- To provide right information to the right user at the right time.
- To motivate readers to improve their reading habits.
- Provide easy access to learning resources.
- To provide updated information to the library users.
- To achieve minimum 90% user satisfaction.

**Working Hours**

|     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- |
| General | Monday to Saturday | 9:00 AM – 8:00 PM |
| Circulation | Monday to Saturday | 9:15 AM – 4:40 PM |
| During the Exam & Test | Monday to Saturday | 9:00 AM – 8:00 PM |

Generally the library will remain open all institutional working days of the year, except 4 days every year for stock verification.

Library uses KOHA library Automation Software, which supports in-house operations of library such as acquisition, cataloguing, circulation, serials control and OPAC. Database is updated daily.

Smart circulation system is used successfully via Bar-code technology for all the resources and barrower cards.

## Women Cell

#### [ABOUT THE COMMITTEE](/p/women-cell-atme)

Women cell mainly focuses on Women’s empowerment that promotes women’s sense of self-worth, their ability to determine their own choices, and their right to influence social change for themselves and others. Women cell conducts activities throughout the year and gives a platform for the stakeholders to exhibit their talents. Women cell recognises and honours the women achievers working in different fields.

#### [OBJECTIVES](/p/women-cell-atme)

Empower women by Encouraging strong network among members; Providing opportunities for women to share knowledge and exhibit talents; recognizing women achievers.

#### [MEMBERS](/p/women-cell-atme)

#### [MEETINGS](/p/women-cell-atme)

The Member Secretary shall, with the approval of the chairperson of the committee, convene the meetings of the Women Cell at least once in two months and on such other occasions as may be necessary. Member Secretary shall with the approval of the chairperson of the committee prepare the agenda for the meeting. One half of the members shall constitute the quorum, However, if there is no quorum for the meeting up to half an hour, then the meeting shall stand adjourned to the next convenient day fixed. In the adjourned meeting, if there is no quorum for up to half an hour, then the members present shall themselves constitute the quorum and conduct the meeting. Member secretary shall distribute the minutes of the meeting comprising an action list summarizing what was covered, what was resolved and what actions need to be taken for issues requiring further clarification to all the members who participated in the meeting in consent with the chairperson of the committee.

#### [ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES](/p/women-cell-atme)

- Planning the activities for the year before the commencement of the academic year.
- Giving the budget proposal for the upcoming academic year before the end of the current financial year.
-  Conducting a meeting ten days prior to the planned event & having the discussion regarding the action plan & role & responsibility of the individual coordinators towards the conduction of the event.
- Placing a request to the Principal one week before the conduction of the   event along with budget request and other details.
- After due approval, preparation of E-flyer for conducting the event and circulation of the same.
- Publicizing of events.
- Sending circulars to all the Departments.
- Sending Invitation to Chief guest, HODs and to all other stakeholders.
- Conduction of activities by the respective coordinators on scheduled date.
- Collecting the winners, runners list by the respective coordinators.
- Purchase of items required towards the conduction of the event.
- Preparation of agenda for the programme.
- Preparation of the certificates and feedback forms.
- Rehearsal of the programme with student & staff coordinators.
- Conduction of the event.
- Preparation and submission of Press report and Report of the event.
- Preparation of Softcopy of the documents pertaining to the event.
- Submission of statement of accounts & reports to Principal.

## INCENTIVES FOR STAFF

#### [1\. Laptop Financial Assistance](/p/incentives-for-staff)

- College pays laptop cost upfront.

- Staff repays in interest-free installments.


#### [2\. Textbook Publication Awards (With ATMECE Affiliation)](/p/incentives-for-staff)

- ₹25,000 – National reputed publisher (ISBN/ISSN).

- ₹10,000 – International publisher (ISBN/ISSN).

- ₹5,000 – Regional/Local publisher.

- ₹2,000 – International book chapter (ISBN/ISSN).


#### [3\. Journal Publication Incentives](/p/incentives-for-staff)

**_Conditions:_**

- Referred journal; from 2nd paper onwards (calendar year).

- One Scopus paper mandatory for all staff.

- Research-only faculty: 1 Scopus paper/semester.

- Approval from Dean (Research) & Head of Institution required.


**_SNIP-Based Incentives:_**

| **SNIP Range** | **2nd Paper** | **3rd Paper** | **4th Paper** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ≤ 0.50 | ₹10,000 | ₹15,000 | ₹20,000 |
| 0.50–1.00 | ₹12,000 | ₹17,000 | ₹22,000 |
| 1.00–2.00 | ₹14,000 | ₹21,000 | ₹26,000 |
| ≥ 2.00 | ₹30,000 | ₹35,000 | — |

#### [4\. ATMECE Research Award](/p/incentives-for-staff)

- Annual cumulative SNIP ≥ 2.

- 100% weightage – 1st author.

- 50% weightage – 2nd author (Ph.D.-related).

- In collaborations, only one ATMECE faculty eligible (100% weightage).


#### [5\. Conference Support (Within India)](/p/incentives-for-staff)

**_Eligibility:_** _Reputed conferences (IEEE/Springer/ASME/ACM, etc.), reputed host institutions, oral presentation only._

**_Support (First Author):_**

- SCL + Registration (Max ₹8,000)

- TA: Sleeper class or ₹3,000 (whichever less)


**_Key Points:_**

- Only one faculty per joint paper.

- Max 3 conferences/year.

- Student papers: ₹8,000 registration + TA (Max ₹2,000).

- Papers must be Scopus/WoS indexed (or ISBN for Humanities).


#### [6\. Workshops / FDP / STTP / SDP](/p/incentives-for-staff)

**_Eligibility & Limits:_**

- Reputed institutes; preference for AICTE/ISTE (≥5 days).

- Min. 1 year service.

- Max 2 programs/year; 2 faculty/department at a time.


**_Financial Support:_**

- SCL + Registration (Max ₹3,000)

- TA actuals or ₹2,500 (whichever less)

- FDP outside Mysuru: ₹1,000/day (if no boarding/lodging)


**_Conditions:_**

- Attend preferably during semester break (>2 days).

- Knowledge dissemination mandatory after FDP outside.

- Pre-approval required; documents to be submitted within one week after return.

## APPLICATION

[Download Application](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/ATME-BE-Application.pdf)

Interested Candidates may download the application from the above links. Duly filled application forms may be sent to the below mentioned address along with a Demand Draft for Rs. 200/- drawn in favour of “ATME College of Engineering, Mysore” payable at Mysore.

**ATME College of Engineering**

13th Kilometer,Mysore – Kanakapura – Bangalore Road

Mysore – 570 028 , Karnataka

Office-0821-2954081, Prinicipal- 0821-2954011

Telefax : +91-821-2593328

**For admissions contact**

+91 90369 26363

Principal: +91-94482-85641

AAO: +91-94482-85644

PRO: +91-98869-75772

email:enquiry@atme.edu.in

On receipt of the above Demand Draft and Application, the ATME brochure shall be mailed to your specified address.

**Documents to be enclosed for BE admissions**

- SSLC Marks Card (Original)
- PUC Marks Card (Original)
- Transfer Certificate (Original)
- Migration Certificate (CBSE, ICSE Students) (Original)
- Study Certificate (all institutions studied-1st to 12th) (Original)
- Character/Conduct Certificate (all institutions studied) (Original)
- ID Proof & Address Proof (Aadhaar, Passport))
- CET Rank Sheet (Mandatory)/ Comed-K Rank Sheet/ JEE Rank Sheet
- CET Admission Ticket (Mandatory)/ Comed-K Admission Ticket/ JEE Admission Ticket
- Prepare 5 sets of Photocopies of the above documents and get attested by the Gazetted Officer or Notary (3 Copies to be submitted along with Original documents to the College and 2 Copies for Self usage)


CET / Comed-K Admission Order (for CET/Comed-K admissions only)
- Passport size photographs-5
- Stamp Size Photographs-3
- Self-Addressed Postal Envelopes-3

## DYNAMICS - Magazine

A college magazine is an annual publication of a college. As College magazine is an attempt to record all the activities of the students and committee though fit to name the college magazine as “DYNAMICS”. It is a forum through which the young learners of the college express their juvenile ideas and knowledge on different topics. Further, to plan and workout logistics a team of dedicated faculty members from each department joined together to form a Magazine Committee. The college magazine is the culmination of students expression of thoughts, aspirations, talents, emotions and creativity of both faculty and students. It encourages them to think beyond academics and brings out hidden talents like literature, art, photography, etc.

**Venue: KMT Group of Institutions – Wisdom PU College, Kushalnagar**

**Project Activities:**

- Hackathon
- Poster Presentation
- JAM Competition
- Technical Project Exhibition

atme-students-selected-for-smart-india-h.title: ATME Students selected for Smart India Hackathon 2022
atme-students-selected-for-smart-india-h.description: A group of six students from ATME College of Engineering, Mysuru  has  been selected for Smart India Hackathon-2022 Senior Hardware edition Grand Finale. SIH
atme-students-selected-for-smart-india-h.markdown:
[Skip to content](/p/atme-students-selected-for-smart-india-hackathon-2022)

[![ATME College of Engineering](/__l5e/assets-v1/4519b204-1c5c-4570-ad02-6e238e674849/ATME-Final-logo-copy.png)](/p/)

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/Hackathon-22-01.jpg)

A group of six students from ATME College of Engineering, Mysuru  has  been selected for Smart India Hackathon-2022 Senior Hardware edition Grand Finale. SIH 2022 brings the next generation evolution by inclusion of new methodology to inculcate the culture of start up and innovation ecosystem across different age groups. The Hardware and Software edition of Smart India Hackathon 2022 Senior is scheduled from 24th August to 29th August 2022. The Grand finale will be held at the nodal centre – B. S. Abdur Rahman Crescent Institute of Science & Technology, Chennai, Tamilnadu.

Students of ATME College of Engineering, Mysuru are selected for sixth consecutive year in the Hackathon organized by Ministry of Education in association with other ministries.

The selected students are from the Departments of ECE, CSE and ME. The participants are Mr. Fawaz Ahmed Khan – ECE, Ms. Lavita Joyce – CSE, Mr. Hannan Ahmed Khan – ME, Mr. Chandrakanth J – ME, Mr. Padmanabha K – ME and the team is  lead by Mr. Nagraj S – ECE.  The team mentor is Dr. Bhagyashree S R, Professor and Dean – Research, ATME College of Engineering, and Mysuru.

vtu-youth-festival-prathibhotsava-2022.markdown:
[Skip to content](/p/vtu-youth-festival-prathibhotsava-2022)

[![ATME College of Engineering](/__l5e/assets-v1/4519b204-1c5c-4570-ad02-6e238e674849/ATME-Final-logo-copy.png)](/p/)

![](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/VTU-YOUTH-FESTIVAL-PRATHIBHOTSAVA-%E2%80%93-202-01.jpg)

21st VTU YOUTH FESTIVAL, “PRATHIBHOTSAVA – 2022” was organized by BMS College of Engineering, Bengaluru various Cultural and literary event was Scheduled from 29th – 31st July 2022. Based on the screening done at college 10 events were shortlisted and 14 students were selected as participants for the event. Two male faculty managers were accompanied for the event along with students.

Students along with faculties reached BMS College of Engineering, Bengaluru campus on 29th of July morning, followed by registration and settled back at accommodation provided by organizing committee.

[**Report on VTU YOUTH FESTIVAL PRATHIBHOTSAVA – 2022**](https://atme.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/VTU-Fest-PRATHIBHOTSAVA-2K22-Report.pdf)

Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering is organising Inter College Technical fest URJA 2k22 in association with IETE, for Diploma Electronics students on 3rd August 2022 at ATME College of Engineering.

\*Hackathon(6Hrs project building competition)

\*Technical Quiz

\*Project Expo(Exhibition of projects)

#### [Best Teacher - AY 2022-23](/p/best-teacher-awards)

### **Teachers Day and Engineering Day – 2023**

On September 30th  2023, the ATMECE celebrated Teachers’ Day and Engineer’s Day jointly. The event was organized by the Student Affair’s office and was held in the College Auditorium..

The program was inaugurated by Mr. L Arun Kumar, chairman ATME Trust. Other members of  management were also present.

On this occasion, the management congratulated and felicitated the PhD holders in the past academic year. Dr. Vinod Kumar P from EEE dept, Dr. Sunitha Patel from CSE dept, Dr.Pavithra A C and Dr.Shalini Hanok from ECE dept, Dr. Husna Zohara from AI & ML dept, Dr. Shashi Ranjan were felicitated.

Later, considering the academic performance of the staff’s various awards like Best Teacher, Best Technical staff, Best supporting staff was announced.

**Best Teacher: Dr. Prakash Kuravatti, Dept of ECE**

**Dr.Chethan, Dept of ME**

**Mrs. Shruthi H G, Dept of CE**

**Best Technical Staff: Mr. Nannayya, Dept of Admin**

**Best Supporting Staff: Mr. Shivakumar, office**

All the awardees were felicitated by the guests.

The next speaker was Dr. Syed Shakheeb Ur Rahman  the one who spoke about the contributions of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and Sir Mokshagundam Visvesvaraya, two of the greatest teachers and engineers India has ever produced.

Mr. L Arun Kumar in his speech He also praised the faculty members of the institution for their dedication and hard work, and the students for their academic achievements.

During the occasion, principal, Dr. A K Murthy, AO, Dr Sachidananda Murthy, members of ATME Trust Mr. K Shivashankar, Mr. R Veeresh, H Venkatesh, Dr. Dheerendra Kumar Mehta, IQAC Chairman Dr. L Basavaraj were present

The Teachers’ Day and Engineer’s Day celebration was a huge success. It was a great opportunity for the students to express their gratitude to their teachers and engineers, and to learn more about the contributions of these two great men.
